title: Project Assistant (DTM)
body:
Overview of position

Under the overall and direct supervision of the DTM Programme Officer, and in close coordination with the DTM Snr. Programme Associate, the successful candidate’s primary role will be to provide administrative and overall project support for the implementation of the Displacement Tracking Matrix project in Nigeria.

Role objectives

- Assist in the implementation and monitoring of project activities.
- Retrieve, compile, summarize, and present information/data on specific project topics.
- Monitor budget; verify availability of funds; obtain necessary approval and update budget related information.
- Support administrative coordination of project implementation, involving liaison with diverse organizational units and external parties to initiate requests, obtain necessary clearances, process and follow-up on administrative actions, etc.
- Draft status reports, identifying shortfalls in delivery and bringing them to the attention of the supervisor.
- Draft correspondence, reports, briefing notes, graphics, statistical tables, presentations and other forms of documentation.
- Organize meetings, workshops and training sessions.
- Respond to general information requests and inquiries; set up and maintain files/records.
- Perform other related duties as assigned

Project reporting

This role will work under the overall and direct supervision of the DTM Programme Officer, and in close coordination with the DTM Snr. Programme Associate

Key competencies

- Experience in liaising with governmental authorities, national/international institutions, United Nations agencies and non-governmental organizations.
- Experience in working with migrants, refugees, internally displaced persons, victims of trafficking and other vulnerable groups.
- Prior work experience with international humanitarian organizations, non-government or government institutions/organization in a multi-cultural setting is an advantage.
- In-depth knowledge of the broad range of migration-related subject areas dealt with by the Organization;
- Knowledge of UN and bilateral donor programming.
- Knowledge of financial rules and regulations.
- Knowledge of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS).
- Strong logistics skills related to the implementation of project activities.
- Good communication skills and proven ability to work in a team.
- High level of computer literacy (Word, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint).
- Ability to independently carry out tasks.
- Ability to multi-task and prioritize required. ▪ Ability to work effectively with government counterparts.
- Excellent attention to detail and ability to collect statistical information accurately and maintain records.
- Demonstrated ability to maintain detail, accuracy, and confidentiality.
- Ability to work effectively with different levels within and outside the organization and with colleagues from various cultural and professional backgrounds.
- Working knowledge of the local languages in the Northeast, north-west and north-central.
- Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.

Team management

This role has no team management responsibility.

Further information

Females with required qualifications and experience are highly encouraged to apply.

title: Junior Project Assistant
body:
**Introduction**

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates are considered as first-tier candidates.

**Organizational Context and Scope**

Under the direct supervision of the project manager and under the guidance of the Head of Unit for Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion (LMI) and under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission in the Country Office for Belgium and Luxembourg, the incumbent will assist the LMI team with the implementation of projects of the IOM Country Office. In addition to this, the incumbent will be expected to support some activities related to the development of new projects in the LMI Team.

**Responsibilities**

In particular, the incumbent will:

  
I. ASSIST WITH THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROJECTS

1\. In close coordination with the LMI Head of Unit, assist the Project Management Teams with the implementation and follow-up on project activities. This includes supporting the team with research tasks, administrative tasks and the (logistical) organization of meetings and events.   
2\. Assist with the drafting/ formatting of reports; routine correspondence, type letters, reports and memoranda as well as IOM documents and forms related to IOM operational and administrative matters;   
3\. Assist the Project Management Team with the development of new projects and initiatives in the field of Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion. This includes assistance with the drafting/ formatting of concept notes and project proposals.   
4\. Assist in drafting/ formatting public information documents, website articles, press releases and information dissemination on IOM activities towards public and private stakeholders.   
5\. Any other tasks as may be required.

  
II- ASSIST WITH POLICY SUPPORT AND OUTREACH

6\. Assist in identifying possible partnerships with the private sector, civil society (NGOs, diaspora associations, etc.) and other stakeholders (such as the Belgian government and universities) in order to improve knowledge on migration initiatives and policies.   
7\. Assist with the drafting/ formatting of presentations and speeches related to integration for the LMI Head of Unit or the Chief of Mission.   
8\. Prepare for, participate in and follow-up on meetings/conferences on behalf of the organization.   
9\. Any other tasks as may be required.

**Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

**•**  Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in economics, social science, migration studies or related field from an accredited academic institution with one year of relevant professional experience.   
OR   
• Completed High School degree with three years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

• Demonstrated first working experience or internship in the area of project management, or evaluation of projects;   
• Demonstrated first working experience or internship in the area of migrant integration or labour migration;   
• Strong organizational and time-management skills;   
• Ability to work independently;   
• Experience in liaison with non-governmental organizations, national, regional and international authorities and institutions is an advantage.

**Skills**

• Strong organizational and time-management skills;   
• Strong communication and diplomatic skills, applied in a professional environment;   
• Ability to work independently against tight deadlines.

**Languages**

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Advanced knowledge of Dutch is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

**Values** - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

- **Inclusion and respect for diversity**: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- **Integrity and transparency**: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- **Professionalism**: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- **Courage**: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- **Empathy**: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

**Core Competencies** – behavioural indicators Level 1

- **Teamwork**: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- **Delivering results**: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- **Managing and sharing knowledge**: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- **Accountability**: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- **Communication**: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

**Notes**

Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

title: Training Officer, Cultural Orientation
body:
**Job Overview:** The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

The IRC is seeking a Training Officer, Cultural Orientation for Switchboard, an Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR)-funded program. Switchboard is a one-stop resource hub for refugee service providers in the United States. Switchboard provides training and capacity-building services to service providers in the United States, including resettlement agencies and affiliates, state agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others. More information about Switchboard can be found at [www.SwitchboardTA.org](https://reliefweb.int/file:///C:UsersTigestCoAppDataLocalMicrosoftOlkAttachmentsooa-fefcb179-4b91-4707-b044-59e9496f57fe69780562696ebcadf2340c5c93711aeb96e9493d8b84ea912d714b7dd9c61fdbwww.SwitchboardTA.org).

Settle In is Switchboard's digital information service for newcomers taking the knowledge and resources Switchboard offers to service providers and adapting and delivering it directly to newcomers**,** in multiple languages, through its website (SettleInUS.org), mobile app, and social media platforms. More information on Settle In can be found on https://www.settleinus.org/.

Cultural orientation is a core service in refugee resettlement in the United States, helping newcomers build the knowledge and skills to navigate life in their new communities. The Training Officer, Cultural Orientation, leads the development and delivery of capacity-building initiatives for these programs. This includes training and technical assistance (TTA) to service providers, helping them build strong cultural orientation programs and apply best practices when working with newcomers. This staff member is responsible for producing and maintaining high-quality performance by collaborating with experts, designing effective cultural orientation resources such as curricula, training materials, and learning tools, and facilitating learning experiences that improve outcomes for newcomer children, adults, and families. This role requires hands-on experience working directly with clients, subject matter experts, and partners, along with prior experience delivering cultural orientation to newcomers.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Training and Technical Assistance**

- Design and deliver versatile cultural orientation training to service providers and cultural orientation delivery staff.
- Provide responsive and cross-disciplinary technical assistance to refugee service providers in response to cultural orientation TTAs, adapting content to meet varied organizational needs and learning styles.
- In collaboration with colleagues across teams, develop written and multimedia learning resources (e.g., toolkits, videos, podcasts) that reflect trauma-informed, client-centered, and strength-based approaches.
- Adapt materials for different literacy levels, languages, and cultural contexts
- Integrate feedback from internal and external reviewers to continuously improve training and resource contents and delivery methods.
- Facilitate communities of practice and peer learning groups to promote knowledge exchange and cross-training across service areas.

**Project Management**

- Contribute to the creation of Switchboard’s annual training and technical assistance (TTA) workplan.
- Ensure related trainings and learning resources are developed and delivered on time and on budget.
- Use effective communication and collaborative skills with a wide range of stakeholders
- Manage internal and external subject matter expert/consultant relationships and project plans as they contribute to the development of related TTA.

**Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E)**

- Oversee tracking of related TTA outputs and outcomes against targets (materials developed, trainings delivered, individuals participating, etc.)
- Together with Training Officers and Switchboard’s M&E team, review and analyze feedback data from related TTA participants
- Oversee provision of inputs into Switchboard reports, including monthly activity updates and semi-annual Performance Progress Reports.

- Other duties as assigned

**Job Requirements:**

**Required:**

- Bachelor's degree required, preferably in a related field such as Education, International Development, Social Work, Public Administration, Cross-Cultural Studies, Migration/Refugee Studies, or a related social science (or equivalent experience).
- Minimum 6 years of direct service experience with refugees and/or other ORR-eligible populations
- Experience delivering cultural orientation to newcomers
- Experience providing training and/or technical assistance to build the capacity of refugee service providers
- Experience providing client-centered, trauma-informed, and strength-based services for refugees
- Experience in supporting newcomers' access and gaining self-sufficiency for services and resources i.e. financial, medical, social, vocational etc.

**Preferred:**

- Lived experience with forced displacement or shared background with newcomer populations
- Experience managing external subject matter experts and/or consultants
- Experience contributing to project M&E (data collection, management, and reporting)
- Experience with evidence-based programming

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

- Working knowledge of programs and services related to client-centered services for refugees and newcomer families
- Strong understanding of cultural orientation frameworks, refugee/newcomer integration principles, and adult learning principles
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with fluency in English; including engaging public speaking abilities
- Self-starter with ability to work both independently and collaboratively as a part of a team
- Capacity to give and receive constructive feedback
- Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple competing deadlines and efficient time management
- Adequate technology literacy including intermediate knowledge of MS Office Suite (Teams, Word, PowerPoint, Excel), and Zoom, with adaptability to learning new and innovative technology.
- Strong attention to detail

***Language Skills:*** Fluent in written and spoken English***.***

**Working Environment:** This position is a remote working environment. Required domestic travel up to 20%.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $80,000 - $85,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Programme Manager, Slovenia (Europe and Asia)
source: Geneva Centre for Security Sector Governance
body:
At DCAF, we envision a world where democratic sector governance advances sustainable peace and development and human dignity for all.

Our mission is to advance the security of all people through nationally owned, inclusive, and participatory security sector reforms based on international norms and good practices.

DCAF contributes to making peace and development more sustainable by assisting partner states and international actors supporting these states, to improve the governance of their security sector through inclusive and participatory reforms. It creates innovative knowledge products, promotes norms and good practices, provides legal and policy advice and supports capacity‐building of both state and non‐state security sector stakeholders.

DCAF Ljubljana is a permanent DCAF regional office, based in Slovenia. The office is responsible for two main programs: implementation of the Police Cooperation Convention for Southeast Europe (PCC SEE) and Western Balkans Border Security Programme (BSP). With funding from the United Kingdom Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO), DCAF Ljubljana is implementing the project “CHAIN BiH”, a project strengthening sub-national case-building and inter-agency coordination against organised immigration crime (OIC) in Bosnia and Herzegovina, with a focus on Una-Sana Canton, and is looking to employ an experienced, high-performing and positive individual to be our next **Programme Manager (Europe and Asia).**

**Location: DCAF Ljubljana, Slovenia, with frequent travel to Bosnia and Herzegovina \***

**Starting date: November 2026 or upon agreement**

**Work rate: 100%**

**Duration: Fixed-term employment until 31 March 2029, with the possibility of extension \*\***

**The role**

Join DCAF Ljubljana as a Programme Manager, tasked with implementation and management of the project “CHAIN BiH”. Reporting directly to the Director of DCAF Ljubljana office and supported by the Project Officer, you will be responsible for the overall coordination and oversight of a unique evidence-led project.

**Key areas of operation**

**Project leadership**

- Lead the overall implementation and day-to-day management of the project across its inception, field-testing, design and implementation phases, ensuring timely delivery of activities and achievement of project objectives.
- Develop and maintain detailed implementation plans, monitor progress, and proactively address implementation challenges, applying adaptive management as evidence from the field emerges.
- Lead the evidence-gathering and diagnostic work of the project.
- Coordinate project resources, supervise the Project Officer and external experts, and ensure effective collaboration across all project stakeholders.

**Partnership management**

- Maintain close working relationships with the donor and other relevant national and international stakeholders.
- Coordinate the participation of various participants in project activities.
- Facilitate the project’s Practice Review Forum, as well as regular communication, coordination meetings and consultations to support effective project implementation.
- Represent DCAF Ljubljana at project meetings, workshops and other relevant events.

**Monitoring and compliance**

- Monitor project progress against the adaptive results framework, agreed indicators and deliverables using results-based management principles, and ensure that lessons learned inform project decisions.
- Identify implementation risks, maintain the project risk register and develop appropriate mitigation measures.
- Ensure that gender equality and social inclusion, human rights, safeguarding and conflict-sensitivity standards are integrated throughout project implementation.
- Ensure compliance with donor requirements, DCAF policies and applicable project management procedures.
- Monitor project finances in close cooperation with the Project Officer and the DCAF finance and administration team, ensuring sound financial management, value for money and efficient use of project resources.

**Reporting and visibility**

- Prepare high-quality narrative and financial reports for the donor and DCAF management.
- Ensure appropriate project visibility and communication in accordance with donor requirements.
- Maintain accurate project documentation and support internal and external monitoring, evaluation and audit processes.

**Your experience**

We are looking for a motivated and experienced project management professional who combines strong organisational skills with the ability to build trusted partnerships across diverse institutional environments.

You bring

- University degree (Bachelor’s or higher) in a relevant field (e.g., security studies, law, criminology, social studies, international relations or related disciplines)
- 7 years of professional experience, including a minimum of 5 years of experience with international project management/implementation
- Proven experience in the planning, implementation and coordination of international projects;
- Experience with project monitoring, evaluation and results-based management, adaptive management and risk management
- Experience preparing high-quality narrative and financial reports for international donors;
- Proven experience in stakeholder coordination, building of partnerships and partnership management
- Demonstrated expertise in one or more of the following areas: organised crime, migrant smuggling and/or trafficking in human beings, criminal investigations, border policing or international police and judicial cooperation
- Experience in designing and delivering capacity-building activities for law enforcement and/or criminal justice institutions
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to work independently and collaboratively in multi-cultural environments
- Professional working proficiency in English and Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian

**Desirable assets**

The following would be considered an advantage:

- Previous experience as law enforcement officer or border police
- Familiarity with the institutional structure and operational aspects of law enforcement and prosecution services in Bosnia and Herzegovina, including at cantonal level
- Experience in working with the Border Police of Bosnia and Herzegovina, SIPA, the Service for Foreigners’ Affairs, the Ministry of Security of Bosnia and Herzegovina and/or cantonal police and prosecutors
- Knowledge of the migration context in Una-Sana Canton
- Familiarity with UK Government (FCDO)-funded programmes or other bilateral donor-funded projects
- Experience in integrating gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) and human rights considerations in security sector projects
- Experience working with international organisations or EU-funded programmes
- Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office tools, particularly Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook

**We offer**

At DCAF Ljubljana, you will have the opportunity to contribute to a project that supports more effective, rights-based responses to organised immigration crime and stronger security sector governance in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

We offer:

- an opportunity to work on a high-impact international project with tangible regional impact
- a rewarding, dynamic and meaningful work experience
- the chance to be part of a diverse team of collaborative, respectful, hardworking and values-driven people
- opportunity for professional growth, international networking and continuous learning
- the chance to contribute to advance the security of all people through nationally owned, inclusive, and participatory security sector reforms based on international norms and good practices

***\* The post holder is expected to undertake frequent travel to Bosnia and Herzegovina, in particular to Una-Sana Canton.***

***\*\* The post remains subject to continued project funding.***

title: 23302 Head of Partnership and Programme Support Unit (P)
body:
Under the direct supervision of the Chief of Mission (COM) and in close coordination with the Head of Programmes (HOP) and relevant units at country, regional and headquarters levels, the Head of Partnership and Programme Support Unit will be responsible for managing the Unit, which encompasses Programme Development and Reporting, Strategic Communications, Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL), and Information and Knowledge Management.

The Head of Partnership and Programme Support Unit will support the COM and HOP in strengthening mission-wide programme quality, portfolio coherence, strategic planning, resource mobilisation, donor engagement and internal coordination. This includes oversight of the project pipeline, proposal development, donor and institutional reporting, partnership intelligence, evidence generation, quality assurance, compliance-sensitive documentation, and contributions to UN, government, and inter-agency frameworks, in line with IOM standards and the One UN approach.

**Responsibilities and Accountabilities**

1. Support the Chief of Mission (COM) and Head of Programmes (HOP) on the Country Office’s (CO) strategic planning and positioning, including the development of strategies, appeals and other strategic submissions aligned with IOM global and regional priorities, the Strategic Results Framework, Rwanda’s national priorities and relevant UN frameworks.
2. Support the CO's resource mobilisation efforts by analysing migration trends, donor and country policies and priorities, funding opportunities and partnership entry points, and defining and implementing proactive fundraising strategies in coordination with Programme Managers and relevant units.
3. Lead the development and implementation of the CO’s donor and partner outreach approach, maintaining strategic dialogue with existing and prospective partners and positioning the Mission’s priorities.
4. Coordinate and oversee development of MEAL systems in line with IOM’s Strategic Results Framework (SRF) to put forth mission-level results-based management, ensuring that results, deliverables, risks and performance trends are assessed, and that evidence and lessons inform programme quality, strategic planning and adaptive management.
5. Support policy, government liaison and external engagement functions, ensuring consistency of institutional messaging, adherence to reporting and escalation protocols, and alignment with the CO's strategic priorities.
6. Coordinate CO contributions to UN, government and inter-agency planning, programming and reporting processes, including the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework and other relevant national, regional and institutional frameworks.
7. Lead programme and project development, including concept notes, proposals, results matrices, budgets, appeals and Project Information and Management Application (PRIMA) submission packages, ensuring a results-based approach and compliance with IOM standards, donor requirements and internal clearance processes.
8. Maintain strategic oversight of the CO’s project portfolio and pipeline, including reporting obligations, revisions, extensions, closures, expenditure trends, delivery constraints and key risks; maintain mission-level project information, management dashboards, institutional records and lessons learned; and ensure timely analysis, escalation and follow-up with the HOP, Resources Management Unit (RMU) and Programme Managers.
9. Oversee donor and institutional reporting and quality assurance processes, ensuring that proposals, reports, strategic documents and visibility products are accurate, evidence-based and compliant with IOM standards, donor obligations, data protection requirements and institutional clearance procedures.
10. Manage the Partnership and Programme Support Unit and provide strategic oversight of its Programme Development and Reporting, Strategic Communications, Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning, and Information and Knowledge Management functions, ensuring coherent work planning, supervision and timely support to programme teams.
11. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Political or Social Science, International Relations, International Development, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in programme development, donor reporting, strategic planning, results-based management, resource mobilisation and project cycle management in humanitarian, development or migration-related contexts;
- Experience supervising staff and coordinating cross-functional teams, including reporting, MEAL, communications, donor relations or knowledge management functions; and,
- Experience liaising with donors, government counterparts, United Nations agencies and internal institutional stakeholders, including Regional Office (RO) and Headquarters (HQ), is required.

**Skills**

- Strong knowledge of programme quality, proposal development, donor reporting, portfolio monitoring, compliance and results-based management;
- Advanced research, writing, outreach and communications skills;
- Good understanding of MEAL concepts, results frameworks, indicators, evaluation planning, data quality assurance and learning processes; and,
- Demonstrable knowledge of Rwanda’s political, development, migration and humanitarian context.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

title: 23257 Chief Migration Health Officer (P)
body:
Under the direct supervision of the Chief of Mission (COM), and the technical supervision of the Regional Health Assessment Programme Coordinator (RHAPC) and in coordination with the Head of Programmes and the Regional Migration Health Specialist for your region, the Chief Migration Health Officer will be responsible for the development, implementation, and management of the Health Assessment and other health programmes.

**Responsibilities and Accountabilities**

**Health Assessment Portfolio**

1. Organize and supervise the migration health assessment process to fulfil the technical requirements of the resettlement countries in the areas of:
    
    1\. Medical examinations
    
    2\. Imaging
    
    3\. Laboratory testing
    
    4\. Vaccinations
    
    5\. TB management
    
    6\. Treatment and referrals
    
    7\. Pre-departure procedures and medical movements
    
    8\. Documentation, certification and information transmission
    
    9\. Other technical areas as may be required
2. Ensure that the infrastructure and equipment of Health Assessment Programme (HAP) premises meet professional standards of quality and safety and are sufficient and adequate for the provision of the services.
3. Ensure that human resources and HAP organizational structure are sufficient and adequate for the planned levels of health assessments and that the staff have the necessary qualifications and skills. Establish a sufficient network of external human resources, such as consultants and medical escorts, to support the health assessment process and travel assistance. In coordination with the Human Resource Unit, ensure that all medical personnel maintain valid licenses to practice.
4. Ensure that the regulatory government authorities are informed about IOM’s health activities and that the IOM medical facilities have obtained approval to provide health assessments and related services.
5. Establish and maintain efficient, client-centered procedures and ensure a high level of integrity at all stages of the HAP process, including client information and appointment system, payment, registration, pre- and post-test counselling, examination, testing, treatment and referrals, submission of health assessment results, pre-departure and other procedures. Establish and maintain a system enabling clients to provide feedback.
6. Establish and maintain a system of quality improvement for each service area. Undertake quality control activities on a regular basis; practice observation and regular supervisory visits to all facilities/teams involved in the health assessment operations. desk audits and use self-assessment tools. Use data analysis and a web reporting system to monitor performance indicators. Ensure implementation of the global IOM Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs); create and implement country-specific SOPs for each service area. Ensure proper reporting and management of incidents according to the Guidance Note for Incident Management.
7. Incorporate additional public health interventions in the HAP context. Such interventions may include surveillance for communicable diseases, outbreak preparedness and response, health education and health promotion, public health services for host communities, liaison with public health institutions, and other activities.
8. Supervise health and non-health staff as well as external consultants involved in the health assessment process; ensure that performance evaluations for health staff are completed in a timely manner. Ensure that all staff are aware of the IOM Standards of Conduct under Article 42, and continuously reinforce these standards. Inform in due time the COM and the IOM Ethics Committee of any issues regarding staff misconduct.
9. Establish the HAP staff development strategy and ensure that the appropriate plan is implemented. Within that plan, apart from attendance at external educational events, initiate, organize, and deliver various professional in-house trainings.
10. Liaise with external service providers to negotiate agreements in coordination with the Resource Management Officer (RMO). To the extent possible, exercise quality control over outsourced services and take corrective measures if necessary.
11. Liaise with relevant partners at government level, immigration and health authorities of the receiving countries, as well as other international UN and non-UN agencies, Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), donor community and national partners.
12. Maintain confidentiality and security of migration health data in accordance with the IOM Data Protection Principles.
13. Organize systematic collection, processing, and analyses of migration health data. Ensure data quality. Provide periodic, as well as ad hoc reporting to the Migration Health Division (MHD) for Migration Health (MH) activities.
14. Oversee the financial aspects of the health programmes in close coordination with the mission's finance staff: supervise budget preparation and ensure monitoring of MH projects, suggest adjustments and cost-effective solutions, and review financial reports.
15. Provide oversight and coordinate procurement of medical equipment, vaccines, medications, and other medical supplies in coordination with the resource management unit.
16. Organize and supervise activities of mobile medical teams, if applicable.

**Other Health Activities**

1. In coordination with the Head of Office (HOO)/COM, reinforce partnerships and liaise with the Migration Health (MH) sector with the Ministry of Health, health institutions and academia, as well as other relevant leading agencies. Incorporate multi-sectoral approaches to partnerships, as well as capitalize on IOM strengths across all service areas within the overall framework of IOM’s 12-point Strategy adopted by IOM Member States (June 2007).
2. Conceptualize, develop and implement appropriate migration health-related projects that may benefit migrants, Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and host communities as well as conflict/natural disaster affected population in coordination with relevant Units, the Regional Thematic Specialists (RTSs) and other colleagues.
3. Facilitate the integration of health assessment activities into the overall migration-related programming of the Country Office through close collaboration with the various units at the Country Office level.
4. Advise IOM colleagues on the link between the Health Assessment Programme with the two other core MHD programme areas - Health Promotion and Assistance to Migrants, and Migration Health Assistance to Crisis-Affected Populations.
5. Identify opportunities for expanding migration health activities and programmes by informing embassies and consulates of IOM’s migration health work and lobbying for IOM Migration Health Assessment Centres (MHACs) becoming panel sites for Migration Health Assessments (MHA), responding to announcements for calls for proposals by drafting project concept notes and/or proposals and liaising with UN agencies and the Ministry of Health to identify project development opportunities.
6. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- University degree in Medicine from an accredited academic institution with preferred specializations: internal medicine and its subspecialties, Paediatrics, Anaesthesiology, Emergency Medicine, Family Medicine, Obstetrics and Gynaecology; and a minimum of nine years of relevant professional experience, of which at least three years of managerial responsibilities; or,
- University degree in Medicine from an accredited academic institution with preferred specializations: internal medicine and its subspecialties, Paediatrics, Anaesthesiology, Emergency Medicine, Family Medicine, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, plus Master’s Degree in Community or Public Health, Medical Specialization in Infectious Diseases, Tropical Medicine, or other related fields from an accredited academic institution, with seven years of relevant professional experience, of which at least three years of managerial responsibilities.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Professional continuous clinical experience, preferably in a multidisciplinary hospital setting or at IOM/similar international clinic context;
- Experience in Migration Health Assessments;
- Demonstrated progressive experience in health programme management;
- Experience in project development, management, and report writing; and,
- Experience in migration health emergency response is an asset.

**Skills**

- Effective managerial and leadership skills;
- Proven abilities to establish partnerships with government institutions, health institutions, and other partners;
- Knowledge of public health;
- Demonstrable knowledge of patient safety and infection prevention and control;
- Organizational skills; and,
- Communication skills.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

title: 23229 Head of Programmes (P)
body:
IOM has been engaged in migration management in Guinea for over two decades, supporting both national authorities and vulnerable populations through various programmes in migration, development, and humanitarian sectors. The Head of Programmes position is a senior management role within IOM's Country Office in Guinea. This critical position ensures the strategic and operational alignment of IOM's migration-related programmes in Guinea, which face complex and interconnected migration challenges. The Head of Programmes leads a broad portfolio that includes migration management, youth employment, immigration governance, public health, climate change, crisis response, disaster risk reduction, and peacebuilding. This role requires close coordination with national governments, UN agencies, donors, and local communities to ensure that programmes are relevant, impactful, and sustainable.

In addition to overseeing IOM's operations in Guinea, the Head of Programmes will lead the UN Network on Migration for Guinea, driving collaborative efforts to implement the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly, and Regular Migration. This requires building partnerships among UN agencies, government authorities, and civil society to address migration challenges comprehensively.

Given the extensive scope of this position, the Head of Programmes must work with high levels of autonomy under the supervision of the Chief of Mission, exercising strategic judgment to drive the mission's objectives while adhering to IOM’s global standards, donor agreements, and local contexts. Strong leadership, innovative thinking, and the ability to manage complex, multi-country operations are essential for this role.

**Responsibilities and Accountabilities**

1. **Strategic Leadership and Programme Management**  
    **•** Lead the development and implementation of country strategies for Guinea, ensuring programmatic interventions are cohesive and aligned with migration-related challenges. Areas of focus include:  
    **•** Labor Migration and Youth Employment: Oversee initiatives aimed at promoting job creation and skills development for vulnerable youth populations.  
    **•** Immigration and Border Governance (IBG): Lead IBG projects, including capacity-building for national authorities in border management and counter-trafficking.  
    **•** Crisis Response and Disaster Risk Reduction: Direct crisis response efforts and manage disaster risk reduction initiatives.  
    **•** Community Stabilization and Peacebuilding: Lead peacebuilding projects focusing on community cohesion, particularly in conflict-affected regions.  
    **•** Migration Health: Ensure the effective delivery of Migration Health Assessment Center (MHAC) services and public health support for mobile populations.  
    **•** Coordination and Integration: Harmonize programming across Guinea to achieve regional impact.  
    **•** Human Resources and Capacity Development: Supervise and mentor program staff, fostering a learning environment for continuous knowledge-sharing and capacity-building.  
    **•** Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL): Oversee robust monitoring systems to track program outcomes, ensuring transparency and accountability.
2. **Partnerships and Resource Mobilization**  
    **•** Donor Engagement: Lead resource mobilization efforts to secure funding from key donors, including the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), the European Union (EU), Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA), Swiss Development Cooperation, and others.  
    **•** Partnership Development: Build relationships with government counterparts, UN agencies, Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), the private sector, and civil society organizations to enhance IOM’s impact.  
    **•** Coordination with UN and Humanitarian Agencies: Represent IOM at UN forums and inter-agency meetings, ensuring migration issues are prioritized in development and humanitarian agendas...  
    **•** Cross-Border Initiatives: Develop cross-border projects, particularly in peacebuilding, migration governance, and community stabilization, aligning efforts with Guinea and neighboring countries.
3. **Policy Development and Advocacy (10%) and Leadership of UN Network on Migration**  
    **•** Policy Leadership: Support capacity-building and policy dialogues on migration governance at the national and regional levels.  
    **•** UN Network on Migration Leadership: Lead the UN Network on Migration for Guinea, aligning with the Global Compact for Migration. Foster collaboration with UN agencies, government representatives, and civil society to support migration priorities.  
    **•** Migration Policy and Data: Lead migration data collection efforts, ensuring evidence-based approaches inform national and regional migration policies.  
    **•** Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA): Ensure robust PSEA mechanisms across all IOM projects and lead staff training on safeguarding.
4. **Additional Responsibilities:**  
    **•** Oversee the management of programme-related budgetary, financial, and administrative functions in coordination with the Resources Management Unit (RMU).  
    **•** Ensure compliance with donor requirements, conducting programme assessments and evaluating impact.  
    **•** Perform such other duties as may be assigned

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master's degree in Political or Social Sciences, Business Administration, Migration Studies, International Relations, Law, or a related field with seven years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with nine years of relevant experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Proven experience managing large, complex programs in migration management, governance, peacebuilding, immigration and border management, youth development, counter-trafficking, or similar fields;
- Demonstrated ability to lead and supervise multidisciplinary teams;
- Familiarity with the West African context and migration issues;
- Strong resource mobilization and donor engagement experience;
- Demonstrated staff management experience, including staff evaluations; and,
- Extensive experience in training and capacity building.

**Skills**

- Proven leadership in strategic program development and implementation;
- Excellent partnership-building skills with government, UN agencies, and civil society;
- Familiarity with IOM/UN project management cycles and donor requirements;
- Knowledge of UN and bilateral donor programming;
- Capacity to interface with government officials and stakeholders on migration issues; and,
- In-depth knowledge of migration-related issues and policies.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

title: 23233 Media and Communications Officer (P)
body:
Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (COM) in Conakry, Guinea, and the direct collaboration with the Programme/Project Managers, and in close coordination with the Media and Communications Unit (MCU) at the Regional Office (RO) of West and Central Africa in Dakar and the Media and Communications Division (MCD) in Geneva, the Media and Communications Officer will assist with the implementation of internal and external communication and media-related activities for IOM in Conakry, Guinea. In light of the rise in irregular migration and the abuses suffered by migrant’s en-route, notably in Libya, the scale of IOM’s response in West Africa is growing exponentially. The successful candidate will support the preparation and coordination of communications outputs from migrants who have been returned voluntarily to their countries of origin, to share such stories with the communities, the media, the general public, and internally within IOM, with a focus on awareness-raising in Conakry, Guinea.

**Responsibilities and Accountabilities**

1. Facilitate the proper coordination of the awareness-raising strategy in the country.
2. Recommend and organize outreach activities and assist the Chief of Mission in carrying out initiatives that promote IOM’s image and increase the awareness of IOM activities in the country.
3. Inform the Chief of Mission and Programme/Programme Managers on media and communication issues/campaigns.
4. Participate in inter-agency media and communication working groups to encourage information flow across agencies and to contribute to the development of complementary media strategies.
5. Inform field and programme staff in the sub-offices on issues relating to public information and media and communication.
6. Contribute to the design and preparation of appropriate information campaigns for a variety of target groups. Draft detailed cost projections and timelines for executing each element of the strategy.
7. Utilize social media communication tools (including but not limited to Twitter, Facebook, IOM website) to increase awareness of IOM’s work in Conakry, Guinea.
8. Participate in Country Office (CO) key events and workshops and undertake field duty travel as needed in order to acquire material, including photographs of work being undertaken in the field, that would promote IOM with donors and governments.
9. Check that all multimedia materials used in the public domain have the necessary consent forms on file, including digital consent forms through use of the Community Response App.
10. Work closely with Media and Communication Division in Headquarters (HQ) to coordinate news stories, features and Global campaigns.
11. Liaise closely with IOM Conakry, Guinea Programme/Project Managers to regularly update the CO website.
12. Assist the Programme Unit with regular reporting, infographics and situation reports.
13. Contribute to the development of IOM communications strategy for communicating about irregular migration, including development of a centralized system for knowledge sharing and information management.
14. Check that there is appropriate gender parity and awareness in all IOM communications.
15. Contribute towards the coordination of IOM’s media outreach with the UN Humanitarian Communications team and other international and news agencies.
16. Coordinate the development of social mobilization strategies and tools to strengthen information campaigns in Ebola-affected areas.
17. Contribute towards the production of various media resources for affected populations based on key messages and concerns in the context of the Joint Initiative project (funded by the European Union).
18. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Mass Communication, Journalism, Public Information, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in media and communications;
- Previous experience in writing and reporting in international and crisis contexts; and,
- Practical experience in multitasking, prioritizing, and working independently.

**Skills**

- Proven ability to produce quality work accurately and concisely according to set deadlines;
- Strong organizational and editorial skills;
- Ability to understand the Organization’s structure and portfolios; and,
- Ability to work effectively and harmoniously in a team of colleagues of varied cultural and professional backgrounds.

**Languages**

For this position, English and French is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) and/ or a West African language is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

title: Country Director - JRS Thailand
body:
**Position Title: Country Director, JRS Thailand**  
**Location: Bangkok, Thailand with possibility to move Chiang Mai**  
**Reports to: Regional Director, JRS Asia Pacific**  
**Starting date: January 2027**  
**Type of Employment: Localised position open for all nationalities**  
**Local salary package, individual medical insurance, and visa support.**

(Note on family status: This is typically structured as an individual/non-family posting given the inclusion of "individual insurance" and local contract terms, but we need to explicitly add "Non-family posting" or "Family posting" at the top of the ad for absolute clarity.)

**Contract duration: 2 years (possibility of renewal)**  
**Starting Salary: THB88,495-THB102,141 (depending qualification)**

Jesuit Refugee Service (JRS) is an international Catholic organization, with a mission to accompany, serve, and advocate for refugees. Our advocacy flows from a service that is direct, pastoral, human and exposed to the sufferings and limitations of refugee life. Through our presence we help to sustain the goodness and hope in people who live in situations of evil and who have reason to despair. To support such an approach, JRS welcomes people who are able to contribute to and draw from the mission of JRS and the desire to share in the lives of the people we serve.

In Thailand, JRS serves refugees, asylum seekers and other forcibly displaced persons in urban Bangkok Metropolitan Area (BMA) and in two camps in Mae Hong Son. The field offices are located in Bangkok and Mae Hong Son, while the country office in Bangkok with a possibility to move to Chiang Mai. The main areas of work include education, psychosocial services, livelihoods, and advocacy.

**Overall Position Purpose:**

As the leader of JRS operations in Thailand, the Country Director oversees the overall management and success of country programmes, personnel, and offices to fulfill the JRS mission and humanitarian sector standards. Reporting directly to the Regional Director, the role provides strategic management support to project directors and teams while driving country-level operations. Key responsibilities include exploring emerging needs of refugees as well as emerging opportunities, developing and implementing project proposals as participatory as possible, overseeing country finances, evaluating projects, managing staff recruitment and care, managing partnerships especially critical for JRS Thailand’s work in Thailand, and maintaining vital external relations with the local Church, the Society of Jesus, government authorities, and international organizations.

**Responsibilities**

**Provision of Strategic Direction**

- Safeguard and promote the mission, vision, identity, values, and unity of JRS across all programmes in Thailand.
- Monitor political, social, economic, and migration trends to formulate proposals for new initiatives, project designs, and advocacies responding to the greatest needs of refugees and displaced persons.
- Lead the development and implementation of country strategic plans that is translated into annual programming, financial budgets, and in-country policies with participation and consultation of the staff.
- Facilitate critical reflection, monitoring, and evaluation of JRS projects to continuously improve program quality and services.
- Provide direction and guidance for JRS Thailand advocacy in country, in collaboration with JRS Asia Pacific and Global Offices.
- Identify capacity development/strengthening needed by the staff to do their roles
- Act as the gatekeeper of the JRS communication strategy and products to ensure. risk management, submitting required reports to Regional Director.

**People Management & Care**

- Review HR needs against available resources to ensure effective and efficient service delivery.
- Provide leadership, inspiration, and holistic care for staff well-being, fostering a supportive, multicultural, and professional working environment.
- Guide and support field teams through regular visits and listening sessions to maintain high standards of quality and accountability.
- Oversee staff recruitment, contracts, appraisals, and terminations in collaboration with HR and Project Directors.
- Lead regular reviews and updates of JRS Thailand’s Personnel, Travel, and Child Protection and Safeguarding policies.

**Programming**

- Guide the programming strategy to adapt to dynamic contexts for urban and in-camp refugees, as well as other emerging displacement issues aligned with the JRS mission.
- Collaborate with the Country Programme Officer, Project Directors, and Finance Manager to design proposals addressing the evolving needs of displaced populations.
- Ensure all projects comply with donor partnership agreements and humanitarian sector standards.
- Oversee timely and accurate reporting on project progress, challenges, and field updates through six-month and annual reports.
- Maintain regular communication with field teams to share critical updates regarding government policies, refugee situations, and organizational developments.
- Oversee database development and management to ensure data used for program development and reporting is accurate, while maintaining strict protection for sensitive information.

**Operations (Finance, Administration & Procurement)**

- Ensure financial administration and procurement strictly adhere to JRS policies to maintain full accountability.
- Lead the annual country planning and budgeting process collaboratively alongside the Finance Manager, Project Directors, and key staff.
- Oversee annual project and institutional audits, implementing corrective actions based on auditor recommendations in consultation with the Finance Manager and relevant team members.
- Monitor project budgets and financial reports, actively overseeing funding status and managing re-budgeting processes as needed.

**Partnership Management & Representation**

- Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with the local Jesuit Provincial, diocesan Church, local Jesuit communities, government authorities, key NGOs, and UNHCR.
- Sustain existing partnerships and forge new ones to ensure JRS Thailand's mission remains context-driven and responsive to the evolving needs of the communities we serve.
- Works closely with CCSDPT representatives and other NGOs in Thailand, UNHCR and the Royal Thai government at national level. JRS together with other organizations and networks also advocate changes to government policy/practice as needed for the benefit of the refugees.
- Represent JRS at national-level meetings with NGOs, UNHCR, government bodies, and stakeholder forums.
- Ensure prominent representation in donor forums while strictly complying with Thai government and donor requirements.

**Qualifications & Experience:**

- Education: Degree in Development Studies, Social Work, International Development, or a related field.
- Experience: Minimum of five years in a senior management role, overseeing complex programs, diverse multi-cultural teams, and strategic partnerships (experience in Asia is an advantage).
- Financial & Technical Skills: Strong background in project cycle management, budgeting, financial monitoring, and accounting, alongside high computer literacy (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
- Communication: Excellent written and verbal English communication skills, with a proven track record in report writing and proposal development (knowledge of Thai is an advantage).
- Values & Mindset: Deep empathy for refugees, a strong grasp of local cultural sensitivities, and a service-minded, patient, and self-motivated approach.
- Personal Attributes: Exceptional diplomatic, leadership, and stress-management skills, with the ability to thrive under pressure in a multicultural, multi-faith, and resource-constrained environment.

title: MMC Consultancy on Sudan Displacement Data Analysis and Report Writing
body:
## Who is the Danish Refugee Council?

Founded in 1956, the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) is a leading international NGO and one of the few with a specific expertise in forced displacement. Active in 40 countries with 9,000 employees and supported by 7,500 volunteers, DRC protects, advocates, and builds sustainable futures for refugees and other displacement affected people and communities. DRC works during displacement at all stages: In the acute crisis, in displacement, when settling and integrating in a new place, or upon return. DRC provides protection and life-saving humanitarian assistance; supports displaced persons in becoming self-reliant and included into hosting societies; and works with civil society and responsible authorities to promote protection of rights and peaceful coexistence.

MMC is a knowledge centre engaged in data collection, research, analysis, and policy and programming on mixed migration. MMC has regional hubs hosted in Africa, Asia, Europe and Latin America, with a global team headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, and based in several countries worldwide. MMC is a leading source for independent and high-quality data, research, analysis and expertise on mixed migration. MMC aims to increase understanding of mixed migration, to positively impact global and regional migration policies, to inform evidence-based protection responses for people on the move and to stimulate forward thinking in public and policy debates on mixed migration. MMC’s overarching focus is on human rights and protection for all people on the move. The MMC is part of and governed by the Danish Refugee Council. For more information on MMC visit our website ([http://www.mixedmigration.org/](http://www.mixedmigration.org/)).

## Purpose of the consultancy

MMC Eastern and Southern Africa, Egypt and Yemen, based in Nairobi, occupies a central place in producing regional research on mixed migration dynamics. In 2026, MMC has a project with UNHCR on the regional and routes-based displacement consequences of the war in Sudan. Three years into the war, displacement dynamics have become increasingly complex, regionalised, and multi-directional. Movements are no longer limited to neighbouring countries but extend across North Africa, the Sahel, the Mediterranean, and beyond, often through non-linear and stepwise pathways.

Existing analysis has highlighted several critical features:

- The vast majority of Sudanese remain close to Sudan, but a growing number engage in onward movement across routes.
- Movement decisions are shaped by shrinking protection space, limited access to services, and deteriorating conditions in countries of asylum, rather than predefined destination intentions.
- There is a need to better understand drivers of movement, protection risks, and decision-making processes over time, rather than focusing only on arrivals or flows.

Both UNHCR and MMC hold complementary datasets:

- UNHCR: protection monitoring (quantitative and qualitative), registration/profiling data, operational insights
- MMC: 4Mi primary data, qualitative interviews, route-level perspectives

This project proposes to move beyond parallel analysis toward a joint evidence-building exercise, combining UNHCR and MMC data to produce protection-sensitive, route-based insights. The joint analysis will lead to comprehensive report on the Regional and Routes-Based Displacement Dynamics linked to the War in Sudan. Key sections will include: 1) analysing the scale of displacement and mapping the various routes, 2) exploring onward movement intentions and decision-making, 3) mapping exposure and identifying the determinants of vulnerability to abuse and harm, 4) mapping assistance gaps and provision, and 5) analysing the scale of returns and return intentions.

Objective of the consultancy

MMC is looking for a consultant to take the lead in:

- Conducting quantitative and limited qualitative analysis, involving the bridging of datasets and methodologies to produce coherent, routes-based and protection-sensitive analysis
- Drafting a joint UNHCR–MMC report on Sudanese (and third-country national) movements across key routes following the outbreak of the war in Sudan
- Informing advocacy, programming, and donor engagement with an evidence-based narrative and presentation of the approach and key findings
- Developing a model of structured data collaboration that can be replicated for other contexts.

## Deliverables

The Consultant will contribute to the following task:

**Phase**

**Expected deliverables**

**Indicative description tasks**

**Maximum expected timeframe**

**Inception**

**1. Data analysis strategy and inception report**

Assess available MMC and UNHCR datasets and draft a plan / inception report for analysing the data, planning data visualisations, and structuring the report. Inception report should include draft sections for the introduction, background and methodology that will feature in the final report.

**5 days**

**Analysis**

**2. Findings presentation**

Full analysis of MMC and UNHCR data, in relation to all research questions; identification of initial findings and presentation to MMC and UNHCR for feedback.

**8 days**

**Writing**

**3. Full draft of report**

Produce full draft of report, following inception report and based on findings developed during the analysis phase. Share with MMC region and global teams and UNHCR for feedback.

**10 days**

**Finalisation**

**4. Final draft of report**

**5. PPT presentation**

**6. Short data analysis brief**

Produce a finalised version of the report, incorporating MMC and UNHCR feedback. Depending on the polished nature of the first draft, this may require more than one feedback round. The final report should be fully copy edited by the consultant and confirm to MMC’s editorial guidelines.

Prepare a powerpoint presentation on the paper’s analytical approach and key findings. The PPT should be framed to inform advocacy, programming, and donor engagement.

Prepare an internal two-page analysis brief on coordinating analysis of MMC-UNHCR data.

**7 days**

The Consultant will provide the completed tasks***by email and in word and powerpoint formats as indicated above.***

## Duration, timeline, and payment

The consultant will work 30 days between November 1st and December 27th, 2026.

DRC will make the first payment of 20% of the total costs upon signing of the contract, and the remaining amount upon satisfactory completion of the work.

## Proposed Composition of Team

- Senior displacement researcher, well versed in qualitative and quantitative data analysis
- Mapping and data visualization assistant, if not a part of the senior researcher’s skillset.
- Copy editor, if needed

## Eligibility, qualification, and experience required

### Essential:

- An advanced degree and post-graduate degree in the Social Sciences, International Development, Migration, Forced Displacement or Refugee Studies, or any other related area of study.
- At least five (5) years of experience in the above or any other related area of study within East Africa.
- Demonstrable experience on matters relating to regional displacement dynamics and migration routes.
- A strong and proven publication track record on migration or forced displacement issues
- Excellent research, analytical and reporting skills.
- Fluency in written and spoken English.
- Prior experience with MMC is a plus.

title: Comprehensive Mapping & Private Sector Analysis (CM&PSA) Consultant
body:
Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

**Project Context and Scope**

Qatar’s Private Sector constitutes a central pillar of the national economy, contributing significantly to economic diversification, innovation, employment and social development.

For the International Organization for Migration (IOM), private sector engagement is increasingly strategic, particularly in advancing sustainable development outcomes, ethical labour practices, and responsible business conduct.

 However, there is currently no single, comprehensive and structured reference that provides a holistic understanding of the private sector landscape in Qatar. Existing information is fragmented, sector-specific, and limited in analytical depth, making it difficult to support evidence-based engagement and decision-making for government entities, UN agencies, and development actors seeking to engage effectively with the private sector.

This consultancy will address this gap by developing comprehensive private sector mapping and analysis, serving both as:

- A public-facing national reference document, and
- An internal strategic resource for IOM to inform engagement and partnership development.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing**

  
The consultant will work under Programmes in IOM Qatar Country Office.  
**Responsibilities**

**Category B Consultants: Tangible and miserable outputs of the work assignment**

The consultant will be responsible for carrying out the following:

**Private sector Mapping**

- Identify and profile major sector companies (large firms, SMEs, multinationals, family businesses, free zone entities, social enterprises)
- Analyze sectoral distribution and typologies across key industries

**Business Associations Analysis**

- Map chambers, councils, networks, and representative bodies
- Assess mandates, membership, and influence

**Corporate Practices and Policies**

- Document CSR, ESG, and sustainability practices
- Assess internal policies related to governance and social responsibility

**Regulatory Framework Analysis**

- Analyze laws and policies governing private sector operations, including:
    - Company registration and licensing 
        - Investment, labour, and governance regulations
        - ESG/CSR frameworks

**Strategic Engagement Component**

- Identify key engagement platforms, events, and communication channels.
- Map companies, business associations, and networks according to IOM engagement pillars (Impact, Income, Innovation).
- Assess organizational interests, capacities, influence, and alignment with IOM priorities.
- Identify and prioritize high-potential partners for strategic engagement, collaboration, sponsorship, technical cooperation, and resource mobilization.
- Develop practical engagement pathways and recommendations for outreach to priority stakeholders.

**Methodology**

The consultant will apply a mixed-method, multi-phase approach, including:

- Desk review of secondary data from official registries, business associations, and company disclosures
- Quantitative data collection through structured questionnaires
- Qualitative analysis of partnerships, engagement potential, and sector dynamics
- Data triangulation (minimum two sources per key data point)
- Use of standardized classification frameworks and data tools
- Stakeholder validation to verify findings

The methodology will follow five phases:

1. Desk review and longlisting
2. Private sector survey
3. Business association mapping
4. Regulatory framework analysis
5. Engagement strategy development

Particular emphasis will be placed on generating actionable findings and practical recommendations that support IOM’s partnership development strategy. The analytical framework will assess stakeholder’s relevance and potential contribution across the Impact, Income, and Innovation pillars, enabling prioritization of engagement opportunities for the Misson,

**Deliverables**

The Consultant will produce the following core deliverables (*on a 5-installment payment basis*):

1. Comprehensive Private Sector Mapping Report
2. Consolidated and searchable private sector database
3. Business associations and regulatory framework annex
4. Internal engagement and strategy annex
5. Executive summary (5-8 pages)

**Duration and Timeline**

Indicative timeline:

- Weeks 1-2: Inception and methodology design
- Weeks 3-5: Desk review and initial mapping
- Weeks 6-10: Stakeholder consultation, questionnaire and landscape mapping
- Weeks 11-14: Analysis and drafting outputs
- Weeks 11-16: Validation and finalization

Each phase will produce interim outputs to support ongoing engagement.

**Reporting and Coordination**

- The consultant will report directly to the designated IOM project manager
- Regular progress updates (weekly or bi-weekly) will be required
- Draft outputs will undergo internal review and validation
- Coordination with:
    - IOM 
        - Government stakeholders
            - Business associations and private sector actors

**Performance Indicators for the Evaluation of results**

The consultant will be evaluated based on:

- Timely delivery of agreed outputs
- Quality, accuracy, and completeness of data and analysis
- Adherence to methodology and data governance standards
- Responsiveness to feedback and stakeholder engagement
- Usability of deliverables for strategic and operational purposes

The consultant must ensure:

- Source transparency for all data collected
- Verification protocols (minimum two-source validation)
- Neutrality and non-endorsement of entities
- Data protection compliance, including informed consent where applicable
- No collection of sensitive or confidential data without authorization
- Screening and mitigation of reputational risks
- All outputs must comply with IOM data protection and ethical standards

## **Qualifications**

**Education:**

- Advanced Masters University degree in a related field

**Experience:**

- Minimum 7 years of relevant experience
- Proven experience in private sector analysis, market research, or economic mapping
- Experience in Qatar or the GCC region strongly preferred
- Familiarity with CSR, ESG, and sustainable business practices
- Experience working with international organizations is an asset

**Skills:**

- Strong analytical and research skills
- Experience in database development and data management
- Excellent report writing and communication skills

**Languages**

For this consultancy, Fluency in English (both oral and written is required) Fluency in Arabic will be considered an asset.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.
