title: Medical Coordinator (F/M) - Afghanistan
body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?

For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

## MdM in Afghanistan

Médecins du Monde re-opened its mission in Afghanistan in 2021 and currently implements programmes in primary healthcare, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), nutrition and harm reduction through a combination of direct implementation and partnerships with local organizations. The mission operates in a complex environment marked by restrictions imposed by de facto authorities, constraints affecting women’s participation and access to services, evolving humanitarian needs and significant challenges for the health system. Current programmes are implemented in Wardak, Farah and Nimroz provinces and place a strong emphasis on community engagement, quality of care and access to essential health services.

## About the role

You will join the mission at a pivotal moment. Beyond ensuring the quality and relevance of medical activities, you will play a key role in strengthening the mission’s medical leadership, supporting teams, reinforcing SRHR priorities and helping to structure programmes, partnerships and ways of working in line with Médecins du Monde’s values and standards. Working closely with the General Coordinator, HQ Health Advisor and programme teams, you will contribute directly to improving access to quality healthcare for vulnerable populations across Afghanistan.

## What you'll do

? Define, drive and monitor the mission's medical strategy and ensure its alignment with MdM's global priorities, with a particular focus on SRHR.

? Ensure the quality, relevance and effectiveness of health, nutrition, MHPSS and SRHR activities across all programmes.

? Lead, support and develop medical teams through coaching, capacity-building and performance management.

? Analyse programme performance and medical data to guide decision-making and continuous improvement.

? Design new projects, contribute to donor proposals and support the mission's strategic development.

? Represent MdM with health authorities, humanitarian actors, partners and community stakeholders.

? Adapt programmes and priorities in response to contextual changes, population needs and humanitarian emergencies.

## Who you'll work with

You will report directly to the General Coordinator and maintain a strong functional relationship with the Health Advisor based at headquarters. You will supervise a technical medical team of two to three people and work closely with programme managers, medical supervisors, support departments and local partners across the mission. The position also requires regular interaction with health authorities, UN agencies, humanitarian coordination mechanisms and community representatives.

## What you'll gain

- Develop advanced leadership skills in one of the world's most complex humanitarian contexts.
- Strengthen your expertise in SRHR programming, community-based health approaches and health system strengthening.Gain significant experience in humanitarian negotiation, representation and stakeholder engagement
- Contribute to meaningful, high-impact programmes supporting vulnerable communities while helping shape the future strategic direction of the mission.
- Propose and develop projects relating to women’s rights and health, in collaboration with local organisations.

### REQUIREMENTS

## You are the right match if you:

- Demonstrate a strong commitment to human rights, non-discrimination and respectful engagement, even in sensitive contexts where values, beliefs or lifestyles differ significantly from your own.
- Can provide strategic medical leadership and bring structure, clarity and direction to complex health programmes.
- Lead teams through trust, listening, accountability and collaboration while fostering a healthy and inclusive work environment.
- Have successfully strengthened the quality, relevance and impact of SRHR or public health programmes.
- Build productive relationships and negotiate effectively with authorities, partners and diverse stakeholders in challenging environments.
- Remain calm, analytical and decisive when responding to emergencies, operational constraints or rapidly changing contexts.

## This role may not suit you if:

- You favour directive or individualistic approaches over collaboration, dialogue and collective problem-solving.
- You struggle to provide constructive management, clear communication and respectful feedback.
- You are uncomfortable representing humanitarian principles and advocating for vulnerable populations in sensitive environments.
- You prefer highly structured and predictable settings over complex and evolving humanitarian contexts.
- You are not aligned with Médecins du Monde's values, principles and activist approach.

## Recruitment process

Apply soon! If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

## Ready to apply?

We only need your CV and a cover letter.

If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we'd love to hear from you!

### **EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: € 3,664
- Fixed-term contract (6 months), starting as soon as possible
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Kabul, Afghanistan
- Regular field visits

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: in a guesthouse with other expatriates initially, with the possibility of individual housing later on
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

title: Team Leader – Evaluation on Humanitarian Assistance, Recovery and Protection in Ukraine Ukraine / Kyiv | Project-based consultancy
body:
**Team Leader – Evaluation on Humanitarian Assistance, Recovery and Protection in Ukraine / Kyiv | Project-based consultancy | Anticipated end 2026–mid 2027**

**About Voluntas (Latin: will, goal, purpose, meaning)**

Voluntas was created from the fundamental belief that all human beings have the inherent right to live a meaningful life.

**That is why we exist: to realize human potential in all corridors of life** – making every workplace, community, and country on the planet full of hope and dignity. Philosophers by heart and advisors by profession, we use our insights to provide evidence-based inspiration, tools and recommendations for our partners around the world.

Voluntas has established offices in Beirut, Copenhagen, Dakar, Kyiv, Mumbai, Nairobi, Port Sudan, and Tunis. We build on a track record of over 270 projects across Africa, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia, serving more than 150 clients. We advise private and public sector actors, including international organizations, government agencies, civil society and foundations, on how to drive meaningful change in societies and organizations.

Our field of expertise is providing fact-based recommendations and policy options grounded in extensive research and data collection in volatile regions and tailored to increase the impact and sustainability of our partners’ efforts.

Voluntas offers a wide range of services across research, policy and governance, including context and thematic analysis, public perception surveys and policy briefs. Under monitoring and social impact, we provide program design, third-party monitoring, evaluations and social impact measurement. We work across thematic areas including agriculture and food, children and youth, economic development, education, gender, health, migration, governance, media, peace and security, and sustainability.

**About the Role**

Voluntas is preparing a tender for an Evaluation on Humanitarian Assistance, Recovery and Protection for an international organization in Ukraine.

We are seeking an experienced **Evaluation Team Leader** to provide overall technical and strategic leadership for the assignment.

The assignment is expected to run from end 2026 to mid 2027 and will assess not only the programme itself, but also the client’s wider contribution to humanitarian, recovery and protection objectives in Ukraine, including areas such as localization, social protection, government leadership, civil society engagement, coordination, and the transition from emergency assistance towards longer-term recovery and resilience. The evaluation will use a theory-based, mixed-methods and contribution-focused approach, with at least four case studies and primary data collection in Ukraine.

**Your Responsibilities**

- Lead the overall evaluation design and implementation.
- Develop the methodology, evaluation matrix, analytical framework and data collection approach.
- Lead theory-based and contribution-focused analysis.
- Oversee qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis.
- Guide case study design and stakeholder engagement in Ukraine.
- Ensure strong triangulation, quality assurance and evidence-based conclusions.
- Integrate gender, disability, vulnerability, ethics and safeguarding considerations.
- Lead key deliverables, including the inception and final evaluation reports.
- Present findings and recommendations to the client and relevant stakeholders.
- Lead and coordinate the wider evaluation team.

**Main Competencies**

- Professional proficiency in Ukrainian is required.
- Minimum 12 years' relevant experience.
- Extensive experience leading complex evaluations in humanitarian, development, recovery, resilience and/or social protection contexts, including conflict-affected settings.
- Strong knowledge of the Ukrainian humanitarian and recovery context.
- Experience with theory-based and mixed-methods evaluation approaches, including contribution analysis, outcome harvesting or process tracing, and international standards.
- Expertise in humanitarian protection, social protection, cash assistance, and/or localization.
- Strong qualitative and quantitative research skills.
- Experience designing inclusive, ethical, trauma-informed data collection with vulnerable populations.
- Experience working with government, civil society, international organizations and donors.
- Proven experience managing multidisciplinary evaluation teams and delivering high-quality evaluations to demanding timelines.
- Excellent analytical, report-writing and presentation skills, including facilitating workshops with senior audiences.
- Excellent written and spoken English.

title: Coordinateur logistique voltigeur - Worldwide (F/H)
body:
Vous souhaitez intégrer une association militante et agir concrètement pour plus de justice sociale ?

Médecins du Monde agit depuis plus de 40 ans pour soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, dénoncer les entraves à l’accès aux soins et faire évoluer durablement les politiques de santé.

En France et dans près de 30 pays, nos actions s’articulent autour de six combats politiques :

- droits et santé sexuels et reproductifs (dont le droit à l’avortement)
- migration, exil, droits et santé
- réduction des risques
- santé environnement
- droits et système de santé
- espaces humanitaires

## **Pourquoi nous avons besoin de vous**

Les interventions d’urgence face aux crises, conflits, catastrophes naturelles, sont l’un des axes prioritaires d’intervention pour Médecins du Monde. Notre indépendance financière, la force de nos partenariats, l'implication et la flexibilité de nos équipes sont autant d’éléments clés pour apporter une réponse efficace à ces catastrophes.

Le mandat de la Cellule Urgence est d’intervenir en priorité sur les urgences et crises qui surviennent dans les pays où MdM est déjà opérationnel (30 pays). La réponse d’urgence dans les pays où MdM n’est pas présent est systématiquement considéré si l’accès au continuum de soins est interrompu et si les capacités du pays et des acteurs sur place sont dépassées.

MdM fournit également un appui et une expertise opérationnelle et technique aux missions des pôles géographiques sur leurs réponses d’urgences.

Vous faites partie de l’équipe voltigeur.euse.s de la Cellule Urgence qui est donc déployée dans les contextes d’urgence pour lancer de nouvelles interventions et/ou renforcer les équipes existantes. Vous pouvez également être déployé.e pour participer à des missions exploratoires, participer à l’ouverture de nouvelles missions et/ou de nouvelles bases, appuyer les opérations/missions existantes MdM à travers du « gap-filling » ou appuyer la mise en œuvre d’activités spécifiques liées aux activités logistiques (ex : formation, préparation, etc.).

## **Vos missions**

Vos principales responsabilités sont :

- Piloter la stratégie logistique de la mission et en assurer la mise en œuvre
- Coordonner et superviser l’ensemble des activités logistiques : chaîne d’approvisionnement, parc de véhicules, gestion des stocks, équipements, bâtiments, infrastructures informatiques, moyens de communication et énergie
- Animer et renforcer les capacités de l’équipe
- Appuyer également le/la coordinateur·rice général·e dans le suivi des procédures de sécurité
- Veiller au respect et à la bonne application des procédures MdM et bailleurs, et contribuer à garantir la qualité, l’efficacité et la conformité des services logistiques au sein de la mission, tout en œuvrant à la prévention et à la lutte contre la fraude et la corruption

Le partage du temps de travail entre le terrain et le siège est évaluée à 80%-20%.

La durée d’un déploiement sur le terrain est de trois 3 mois maximum, et est suivie par un temps de récupération.

## **Vos collègues**

Vous travaillez sous la responsabilité du responsable de la Cellule urgences basé au siège. Lorsque vous êtes déployé.e sur le terrain, vous reportez directement au/à la coordinateur.rice général.e de la mission. Vous avez un lien fonctionnel avec le/la référent.e logistique basé.e au siège. Vous collaborez avec les coordinateur.rice.s support ainsi qu'avec le/la chargé.e d'accès humanitaire & risques et les équipes programme.

## PROFIL

**Vous êtes la bonne personne si :**

- Vous avez une formation supérieure bac+2 type achat ou logistique
- Vous justifiez d'une expérience professionnelle de 5 ans (dont minimum 1 an sur un poste en coordination logistique dans le milieu humanitaire ou de minimum 2 ans d'expérience en tant que logisticien)
- Vous avez une solide résistance au stress et une capacité à vous adapter dans des contextes sécuritaires complexes
- Vous maitrisez le Pack Office
- Vous maitrisez l’anglais et le français couramment à l’écrit comme à l’oral

**Ce poste n'est pas pour vous si :**

- La flexibilité et l’adaptabilité ne comptent pas parmi vos principales qualités ; les déplacements fréquents ainsi que les changements réguliers d’équipe vous posent des difficultés
- Vous craignez de ne pas vous retrouver dans les valeurs et le positionnement militant de Médecins du Monde.

## Les prochaines étapes

Si votre candidature est sélectionnée, nous vous contacterons pour vous proposer un entretien RH avec notre chargée de recrutement. Puis viendront l'entretien technique et managérial (auquel des cas pratiques pourront éventuellement être intégrés).

Dans le cadre de la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme, des vérifications d’antécédents sur listes internationales pourront être effectuées. Les données sont traitées de façon confidentielle et sécurisée. Plus d’infos : [http://bit.ly/3CSThBs](http://bit.ly/3CSThBs)

title: TERMS OF REFERENCE FOR CUSTOMIZATION AND IMPLEMENTATION OF MICROSOFT DYNAMICS 365 BUSINESS CENTRAL
body:
**1.Background**

GROOTS Kenya is a national movement of grassroots, women-led, community-based organizations and self-help groups in Kenya. We were founded in 1995, after the fourth UN Conference on Women in Beijing, China. We aim to address the lack of visibility of grassroots women in development processes and decision-making forums that affect them and their communities.

GROOTS Kenya currently uses Microsoft Dynamics NAV 2017 as its finance management system. The organization intends to migrate to Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central to strengthen financial management, reporting, system integration, automation, data accessibility, internal controls and operational efficiency.

GROOTS Kenya seeks to engage a qualified and experienced consultant toundertake the assessment, design, configuration, data migration, integration, testing, training, implementation, go-live and post-go-live support.

**2. PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT**

The purpose of this assignment is to engage a qualified and experienced consultant to support the organization in planning and implementing and the successfully migration from Microsoft Dynamics NAV 2017 to Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central including assessment, solution design, configuration, data migration, testing and go-live

**3. SCOPE OF WORK**

**3.1 Inception, Current-State Assessment and Requirements**

The consultant shall undertake a comprehensive review of the Organization’s existing systems, processes, data and internal controls, covering finance and accounting, Microsoft Dynamics NAV and Grant Management Information system, budgeting and forecasting, procurement processes, accounts payable and receivable, bank and M-Pesa/mobile money processes, staff and partner advances, fixed assets and inventory, payroll management, tax and statutory reporting, donor and management reporting, financial close processes, approval workflows, user access and segregation of duties, existing system integrations, data structures, reporting requirements and document management. The consultant shall identify inefficiencies, manual processes, duplication, control weaknesses and opportunities for automation.

## **Deliverable**: **Inception Report, Current-State Assessment and Business Requirements Specification.**

**3.2 Fit-Gap Analysis and Future-State Design**

The consultant shall conduct a fit-gap assessment comparing the Organization’s, financial and operational requirements against standard Business Central functionality. Each requirement shall be classified as standard functionality, configuration, extension/add-on, customization, integration, manual workaround or not recommended, with consideration of cost, controls, efficiency, scalability, security, data integrity and sustainability.

The consultant shall also assess the future role of existing systems and recommend whether each system or function should be retained, integrated, replaced, reconfigured or discontinued. Any proposed customization, extension, third-party solution or integration shall clearly outline the solution, costs, risks, dependencies, maintenance requirements and long-term implications.

## **Deliverable: Business Central Solution and Fit-Gap Assessment Report**

**4. FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS**

The Business Central solution shall support, as applicable:

**4.1 Financial Management**

The Business Central solution shall provide comprehensive financial management functionality, including management of the chart of accounts, accruals, prepayments general journals adjustments, multi-currency transactions, bank and cash management, bank reconciliations, accounts payable and receivable, VAT and withholding tax, financial period and year-end controls, audit trails and financial reporting. The solution shall support accurate, timely and auditable financial information and facilitate effective financial controls and reporting.

**4.2 Grant Management**

The solution shall support the Organization’s non-profit and donor-funded operations by enabling financial transactions and reporting to be tracked by key dimensions, including donor, programme, project, activity, department, location, partner/CBO, budget category and restricted/unrestricted funding.

The system shall support grant budget and expenditure tracking, burn-rate analysis, sub-grant and partner expenditure monitoring, and reporting by activity and location. The consultant shall design and implement a practical and efficient financial dimensions and coding framework that meets the Organization’s reporting requirements without unnecessary complexity or duplication.

**4.3 Budget Management**

The Business Central solution shall support annual, programme, project and grant budgeting, including budget preparation, revisions and adjustments, budget version control, budget-versus-actual reporting, variance analysis, commitment monitoring, forecasting and budget availability controls, where appropriate. The system shall provide management with timely information to monitor budget utilization, identify variances and support informed financial decision-making.

**4.4 Procurement**

The solution shall support an integrated procure-to-pay process covering purchase requisitions, approvals, purchase orders/LPOs, receipt of goods and services, invoice processing, payment, accounting and reconciliation. The system shall incorporate appropriate procurement and financial controls, including delegated authority, approval workflows, budget availability checks, supplier controls, invoice validation, three-way matching where applicable, segregation of duties and audit trails.

**4.5 Sub-Grant and Partner Management**

The solution shall support the financial management and monitoring of sub-grants and partner funding, including partner disbursements, partner advances, partner financial reports, liquidations and outstanding partner balances. The system should provide appropriate visibility of partner funding and expenditure and facilitate reconciliation and reporting on partner financial obligations.

**4.6 Fixed Assets and Inventory Management**

The solution shall support the complete fixed asset lifecycle, including asset acquisition, registration, classification, capitalization, depreciation, transfers, disposals, impairment, revaluation where applicable, physical verification and asset reporting. The consultant shall also assess and recommend the appropriate treatment and migration approach for fixed assets, inventory and other non-capital items to ensure that the new system accurately reflects the Organization’s asset management requirements.

**4.7 Payroll Management**

The solution shall support payroll management, including payroll preparation, calculation of statutory deductions and employee benefits, processing of employee changes and generation of employee Payslips. The consultant shall assess the Organization’s existing payroll processes and determine the appropriate Business Central functionality, configuration or integration required to support payroll requirements and statutory compliance.

**5. REPORTING**

The solution shall provide integrated and reliable financial, grant, management and compliance reporting to support operational management, donor accountability and decision-making. At a minimum, the system shall support key financial reports, including trial balances, statement of comprehensive income, Statement of financial position, statement of Cashflows and Statement of changes in net assets, budget-versus-actual, variance analysis, ageing reports, bank reconciliations, and imprest report.

The consultant shall assess existing reporting requirements and configure or develop appropriate reports and dashboards within Business Central or approved reporting tools. Reports shall enable analysis by key dimensions, including donor, programme, project, activity, department, location and partner.

**6. SYSTEM INTEGRATIONS**

The consultant shall assess existing and required integrations between Business Central and relevant systems, including the internal management information system and Microsoft 365/SharePoint. The consultant shall map data flows, identify integration requirements, eliminate duplicate data entry and recommend appropriate integration methods and controls.

The consultant shall configure and test approved integrations, resolve identified issues and provide integration documentation and knowledge transfer. The final integration scope, including data exchanged, frequency, ownership, costs, dependencies and maintenance requirements, shall be agreed during the requirements and solution design phases.

**7. DATA MIGRATION**

The consultant shall develop and implement a structured data migration strategy covering agreed master data, opening balances, outstanding transactions, fixed assets, grants, projects and historical data from the Organization’s existing systems to Business Central.

The consultant shall assess data quality, cleanse and map data, conduct test migrations, and validate and reconcile migrated data against approved source records. Any discrepancies shall be resolved before final migration.

The scope and period of historical data to be migrated shall be agreed during the requirements and solution design phase. Final migration shall be subject to successful validation and reconciliation, with the consultant providing a Migration Completion and Reconciliation Report.

**8. INTERNAL CONTROLS, SECURITY AND WORKFLOW**

The Business Central solution shall incorporate appropriate internal controls, including segregation of duties, role-based access, delegated approvals, automated workflows, user access management, audit trails and controls over sensitive master data.

The consultant shall assess and configure the Organization’s approved control requirements within Business Central and ensure that user roles, permissions and workflows align with responsibilities and delegated authorities.

The consultant shall develop the User Access and Security Matrix, Delegation and Approval Matrix and Workflow Configuration Matrix, and configure and test key transaction workflows, including requisitions, purchases, invoices, payments, journals, budgets and master data changes.

The consultant shall conduct security and segregation of duties testing, resolve identified control weaknesses before go-live and obtain formal Organization approval of user access, security roles and workflows. The consultant shall also provide guidance on ongoing user access management and periodic access reviews.

**9. TESTING AND USER ACCEPTANCE**

The consultant shall develop and implement a comprehensive testing strategy covering functional, integration, data migration, security, segregation of duties, end-to-end processes, UAT and regression testing across key financial, grants, budgeting, procurement, payment, reporting and workflow processes.

The consultant shall provide test scripts, document results, track and resolve defects, and support formal UAT by the Organization. All critical and high-priority defects affecting financial reporting, data integrity, controls, security, compliance or key processes shall be resolved and retested before go-live. A consolidated Testing and UAT Report shall be provided as evidence of successful testing and approval.

**10. TRAINING AND CHANGE MANAGEMENT**

The consultant shall provide role-based training to relevant Finance, Grants, Programmes, Procurement, Management, HR/Administration, ICT and Internal Audit/Compliance users using the Organization’s actual processes and configured Business Central environment.

The consultant shall provide user manuals, process guides, training materials, system administration documentation, frequently asked questions, training records and super-user knowledge transfer to support effective system adoption and sustainable use of the solution.

**11. GO-LIVE**

The consultant shall develop and implement a detailed go-live plan covering final data migration, opening balances, system configuration, user access, integrations, data validation, outstanding transactions, system freeze, reconciliations, contingency and rollback arrangements, go-live activities and formal approval.

**12. POST-GO-LIVE SUPPORT**

The consultant shall provide a **minimum of eight (8) weeks** of post-go-live support covering timely issue resolution, user and configuration support, data corrections, reporting and integration support, system stabilization and process optimization.

The consultant shall provide a clear post-go-live support and escalation mechanism, including designated support personnel, contact channels, issue prioritization and response and resolution timelines

**13. IMPLEMENTATION PERIOD**

The implementation is expected to commence on **1 November 2026** and run through to May 2027, with targeted go-live on **1 April 2027**.

**14. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

1. Demonstrable experience implementing Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.
2. Proven experience migrating from Microsoft Dynamics NAV to Business Central.
3. Experience implementing financial management systems for non-profit, NGO or donor-funded organizations.
4. Experience in financial management systems and accounting processes.
5. Experience with data migration, system integration, testing, and user training.
6. Knowledge of financial controls, reporting, and audit requirements.
7. Relevant Microsoft certifications would be an added advantage.

**15. PROPOSAL REQUIREMENTS**

**Technical Proposal:** Bidders shall submit a technical proposal demonstrating their understanding of the assignment, proposed methodology and solution architecture, approach to Non-Profit Organization and grant management, data migration and system integration, testing and User Acceptance Testing(UAT), training and change management, risk management, implementation schedule, relevant experience, client references and proposed project team, including CVs.

The technical proposal shall also include a detailed implementation workplan, including key activities, milestones, deliverables, dependencies and proposed timelines.

**Financial Proposal:** Bidders shall provide a detailed and itemized financial proposal clearly identifying Business Central licensing, implementation and configuration costs, customization/development, data migration, integrations, reports and dashboards, training, go-live and post-go-live support, as applicable. Bidders shall also clearly distinguish one-off costs, recurring costs, assumptions, exclusions and third-party costs.

Bidders shall clearly identify **one-off costs, recurring costs, licensing costs, assumptions, exclusions and any third-party dependencies**.

title: Senior Data Engineer (Maternity Cover)
body:
**What we are looking for:**

NRC Norway is looking for an experienced **Senior Data Engineer** for a maternity cover position.

You’ll play a key role in building and optimising the data infrastructure that enables NRC to turn complex data into actionable insights. You will design and maintain scalable data pipelines and ETL processes in Microsoft Fabric across data lakes and data warehouses, ensuring that data remains accessible, reliable, and secure. You will also advise on the use of alternative data products when Microsoft Fabric is not the most suitable solution. Working closely with data product managers, analysts and other stakeholders, you’ll translate business needs into effective data solutions, strengthen data quality and governance, and champion modern engineering practices, automation and innovation.

If you’re passionate about data, technology and meaningful humanitarian impact, we’d like to hear from you.

**What you will do:**

- Ensure that data at NRC is accessible and optimized for use in the organisation.
- Instigate collaboration with program managers and field staff to understand their data needs and ensure that data systems are aligned with operational goals.
- Provide technical leadership, support and guidance to non-technical teams on data processing methods and infrastructure setup.
- Implement best practices for data governance, ensuring compliance with relevant regulations and ethical standards.
- Compliance and adherence to NRC policies, guidance and procedures, and a specific responsibility for the functions policies and procedures.
- Build data pipelines in Fabric to integrate internal and external data based on existing internal best

practices. This should reflect the current data needs set by SPK, other operational departments and field operations.

- Contribute to the design and continuous improvement of the Fabric environment, supporting secure data sharing across NRC.
- Contribute to developing the infrastructure, governance, and standards required to make data more discoverable and accessible.
- Build and evaluate systems and data pipelines on Microsoft infrastructure, including Azure and Power Apps, for use cases that fall outside Fabric’s scope, such as archiving solutions, and integrations with other NRC systems.
- Architect the data infrastructure inside and outside of Fabric to ensure it is optimized for performance and can handle the (large-scale) data requirements of the organisation.
- Proactively implement data validation checks, monitoring and error-handling processes to ensure the accuracy, consistency, and integrity of data.

Please download a more detailed [**JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQDKrCT2JlDJS5Zf-TA--9IIAa-KD3fwrJv9-NbZF3szXNU?e=LUSMGu) to learn more about the position.

**What you will bring:**

- Proven experience with IT projects.
- Bachelor’s degree in computer science, software engineering, or related subjects, or demonstrable expertise in the field.
- Advanced analytical skills and problem-solving attitude.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, comfortable working with a geographically distributed team, and can easily work with non-technical colleagues
- Capable of operating in an "Agile" environment
- Fluency in written and spoken English. Other languages are an asset.
- Proactive in keeping up to date with industry trends and innovation.
- 5+ years of experience shipping and maintaining code in production.
- Experience working with Microsoft Fabric or other Microsoft reporting tools.
- Experience or deep understanding of data architecture and data modelling.
- Solid knowledge of programming in Python, fundamentals of API design and security, familiarity with basic DevOps is a plus.
- In depth knowledge and comfortable working with relational databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL) and nonrelational data (JSON format) including building, optimizing, debugging, and creating queries and safe migration scripts.
- Familiarity in working with enterprise information systems in general, and especially ERP and CRM, are desirable.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: NRC Head Office in Oslo, NRC Representation Offices (excluding Geneva and Washington, DC), approved Employer of Record (EoR) countries, and other countries where NRC operates, provided they are within ±2 hours of Oslo time.
- Contract: Maternity Cover (12 Months).
- Travel: Up to 5%.
- Salary/benefits: Grade 9 on NRC’s Resident salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Market Place.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

If you have any questions about this role, please email **ho.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

title: Senior Programme Manager, Academic Pillar (Refugee-Led Research Hub)
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
**Role:** Senior Programme Manager, Academic Pillar (Refugee-Led Research Hub)

**Grade and salary:** Grade 8, £49,119 - £58,265

**Hours:** Full-time 37.5 hours per week

**Location:** Oxford, United Kingdom (minimum 3 days in office)

**Contract type:** Fixed term until 30 September 2028 (with possibility of extension subject to further funding)

**Reporting to:** Head of Programmes (postholder to be appointed, in the interim you would report to the Executive Director)

**Start Date:** 1st January 2026 (desired) but flexible

\*\*Closing date:\*\*19th October (midday UK time) 2026

## **About the Refugee-Led Research Hub**

The Refugee-Led Research Hub (RLRH) supports individuals with lived experience of displacement to become leaders in fields related to human rights, forced migration, humanitarian response and development, politics, and law, among other areas. We do so by delivering academic and professional development programming to a global cohort of students who have been affected by displacement—as refugees, asylum seekers, IDPs, stateless, and beyond—supporting access to graduate degrees and advanced career opportunities. RLRH also creates opportunities for researchers with displacement backgrounds to lead primary and secondary research studies, from start to finish.

RLRH’s team is comprised of colleagues who are deeply committed to advancing refugee leadership, the majority of whom have lived experience of displacement. Our network of staff, researchers, students, and other affiliates is made up of 1,400+ individuals across 80+ countries. RLRH has six active offices: our first was established in Nairobi in 2020, we have had an office at the University of Oxford since 2021, and we have since developed physical hubs in Kakuma refugee camp (Kenya), Kuala Lumpur (Malaysia), Kampala (Uganda), and in the Oxfordshire community (UK).

From October 2025 RLRH is funded to serve as a technical partner for the Mastercard Foundations Scholars Program network, advancing an ambitious global agenda to support displacement-affected learners to access 1,000+ graduate-level scholarships at partner universities around the world. RLRH provides expert guidance and implements specialised programmes to help these learners enter university, thrive on course, and pursue meaningful and enduring careers on completion of their degrees. A complementary, refugee-led research agenda designed by RLRH colleagues produces insights to help Scholars Program partner universities and other stakeholders accelerate positive, long-lasting systems change.

## **The Role**

**Overview of the Academic Pillar:**

The Academic Pillar (AP) manages globally accessible education programmes that reach thousands of bachelors degree-holding refugees, asylum seekers, and others affected by displacement to strengthen their academic credentials and preparedness so they can access postgraduate degrees worldwide. A large, though not exclusive, proportion of the Pillar’s efforts are dedicated to recruiting and preparing African displacement-affected students for Mastercard Foundation’s Scholars Program graduate-level courses at 30+ partner universities. The AP team runs three hallmark programmes to support these prospective students:

**Graduate Horizons** provides learners with comprehensive postgraduate application and admissions support, from selecting right-fit universities and scholarships to crafting compelling personal statements and research proposals. The programme offers hands-on workshops, intensive writing boot camps, one-to-one application feedback, dedicated office hours, and mentorship designed to maximise each student’s academic potential. RLRH actively advocates for students, working directly with universities to eliminate barriers that impede their progress.

A complementary bridging programme that can be completed before or during Horizons is **Graduate Admissions Essentials,** a three-month self-guided programme designed by RLRH to help learners strengthen their academic and professional profiles across the core admissions areas that universities assess for postgraduate study. A wide range of thoughtfully curated resources are available, meeting learners where they are in their tertiary education journeys.

Finally, **RLRH Foundations: Refugee and Forced Migration Studies,** is an intensive nine-module online course that supports students to develop academic skills in the Social Sciences. The interdisciplinary curriculum exposes learners to International Humanitarian Law, Anthropology, Political Theory, Gender Studies, International Relations, and more, preparing participants for study across a wide range of fields of interest. In the near future, RLRH will be developing new Foundations courses, catering to a wider range of subject areas of interest as members of our community prepare for postgraduate degrees.

**Overview of Position:**

RLRH is in an exciting phase of strategic growth. . As the organisation expands its global reach, programme portfolio and operational capacity, we are seeking an experienced senior leader to oversee and further develop our Academic Pillar. The **Senior Programme Manager, Academic Success** will oversee a team of 8+ colleagues across multiple locations, with responsibility for achieving RLRH’s sector-leading objective of supporting **1,000 refugee and displacement-affected learners to enrol in master’s degrees worldwide by 2028**.

The **Senior Programme Manager** will provide strategic, operational and people leadership for RLRH’s Academic Pillar, ensuring that its programmes are coherent, high-quality, inclusive, scalable, data-informed, and delivered with measurable impact. The post-holder will oversee the planning, delivery, governance and continuous improvement of complex academic access programmes, ensuring objectives are achieved on time, within budget and in line with RLRH and University standards.

Working closely with the Head of Programmes, Academic Pillar staff, hub-based colleagues, the MEL team, and other RLRH pillars, the post-holder will lead the operational scaling and strategic development of RLRH’s academic access portfolio. This includes overseeing the effective delivery and expansion of **Graduate Horizons**, **RLRH Foundations**, and **Graduate Admissions Essentials**, with a particular focus on supporting African displacement-affected learners to access postgraduate opportunities across Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program partner universities.

The role will directly manage four Academic Pillar staff: the **Mentoring and Student Success Manager**, **Academic Partnerships and Outreach Manager**, **Academic Content and Facilitation Manager**, and **Senior** **Academic Project Officer**. Through these colleagues, the Senior Programme Manager will oversee the full Academic Pillar learner journey, from outreach and recruitment through academic preparation, mentoring, application support, admissions, transition into study, and longer-term academic progression.

The post-holder will be responsible for strengthening the systems, structures, and ways of working that enable Academic Pillar programmes to operate effectively at scale. This includes ensuring robust programme planning, financial oversight, risk management, data governance, reporting, stakeholder coordination, and quality assurance. The role will be instrumental in embedding a culture of accountability, transparency, collaboration and continuous improvement across RLRH’s academic portfolio.

**Responsibilities**

*Programme Planning, Delivery and Quality Assurance (35%)*

1. Provide end-to-end leadership for the planning, delivery and continuous improvement of RLRH’s Academic Pillar programmes.
2. Ensure that Academic Pillar programmes are delivered on time, to a high standard, within agreed resources, and in line with RLRH’s strategic objectives and University standards.
3. Oversee the full learner journey across the Academic Pillar, from outreach and recruitment through onboarding, academic preparation, mentoring, application support, admissions, transition into postgraduate study and longer-term academic progression.
4. Identify and resolve cross-programme delivery challenges, including timeline clashes, learner engagement risks, communication gaps, capacity constraints and operational bottlenecks.
5. Ensure that programme delivery is coherent across the Academic Pillar’s core areas: outreach and recruitment, academic facilitation, and mentoring.
6. Develop and maintain quality assurance processes across Academic Pillar programmes, including programme reviews, learner feedback loops, delivery check-ins, and mechanisms for continuous improvement.
7. identify opportunities for innovation and future programme development.

*People Management and Coordination (25%)*

1. Line-manage and support a team composed of the Mentoring and Student Success Manager, Academic Partnerships and Outreach Manager, Academic Content and Facilitation Manager, Senior Academic Project Officer and additional support staff based across RLRH's global hubs, setting clear expectations, monitoring performance and providing regular supervision and feedback.
2. Set clear expectations, objectives, and priorities for direct reports, ensuring each colleague has the guidance and support needed to lead their area of work effectively.
3. Convene regular one-to-one and team meetings to support decision-making, resolve challenges and maintain shared accountability across the Academic Pillar.
4. Foster a supportive, inclusive and reflective team culture that values lived experience, professional development, collaboration, mutual accountability and learner-centred practice.
5. Support staff development by identifying learning needs and strengthening colleagues’ skills in programme management, data use, facilitation, partnership management, team coordination and strategic planning through regular performance reviews and professional development conversations.
6. Lead workforce planning for the Academic Pillar, overseeing recruitment, onboarding, succession planning and team development to ensure sustainable organisational growth.

*Strategic Growth and Cross-Pillar Integration (20%)*

1. Translate RLRH’s organisational strategy, Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program commitments and 2028 objective into clear Academic Pillar priorities, annual plans, delivery models and growth pathways.
2. Lead the strategic development and scaling of the Academic Pillar’s programme portfolio, ensuring that growth is realistic, well-sequenced, properly resourced and aligned with learner needs.
3. Advise the Head of Programmes on Academic Pillar priorities, risks, strategic opportunities, partner developments and resourcing needs.
4. Collaborate with peer programmatic leaders across RLRH’s Research and Professional Pathways Pillars to ensure that Academic Pillar programmes connect effectively with research, professional development, alumni and career pathways.

*MEL, Operations, and Budget Management (15%)*

1. Contribute to the development of RLRH’s Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) portfolio, supporting data-driven insights from pillar activities that improve internal programming and contribute to MEL objectives.
2. Lead financial planning, resource allocation and budget oversight for the Academic Pillar, ensuring resources are used responsibly, strategically and in line with grant commitments and organisational procedures.
3. Strengthen operational systems, documentation and knowledge management across the Academic Pillar, including templates, guidance documents, process notes, and playbooks.
4. Ensure that Academic Pillar operations comply with relevant organisational and University policies, including safeguarding, data protection, accessibility, financial management and ethical practice.

*Organisation-wide strategy, learning, and documentation (5%)*

1. Coordinate with Head of Programmes, Director of Operations and Strategy, and Executive Director to input on annual organisation planning.
2. Participate in weekly leadership convenings to influence the strategic direction of the organisation.
3. Represent RLRH at meetings, conferences, partnerships and external stakeholder forums.
4. Contribute to organisation and pillar fundraising and wider grant management needs, as relevant.

## **Selection criteria**

### Required qualifications:

1. A postgraduate degree (or equivalent professional experience). No particular field is expected, but familiarity with (Refugee and Forced) Migration Studies, Education, International Development, and related disciplines can be an advantage.
2. Substantial experience leading complex, multi-stakeholder education, higher education access, widening participation or refugee education programmes, with demonstrated experience managing programme delivery and influencing multidisciplinary teams through line management and/or matrix structures.
3. Demonstrated experience translating organisational strategy into operational delivery through programme design, organisational planning, resource allocation and performance management.
4. Significant experience leading and developing high-performing multidisciplinary teams across multiple geographical locations.
5. Experience working with data, monitoring, and evaluation systems, reporting processes and programme improvement cycles.
6. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to produce clear reports, guidance documents, plans and external-facing materials.
7. Experience building strategic relationships with universities, scholarship providers, NGOs, funders and other senior stakeholders that translate into sustainable programme outcomes and institutional partnerships.
8. Experience supporting programme operations, financial planning, budget management, grant delivery and organisational governance.
9. Commitment to refugee leadership, equity, inclusion and ethical practice.
10. Excellent cultural competence and cultural humility, with experience working effectively across cultures, institutional settings and international teams.
11. Experience working with a high degree of autonomy, exercising sound judgement and accountability within specialist programme areas.

### Desired qualifications:

1. Familiarity with the African education ecosystem and the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program.
2. Fluency in additional languages spoken by RLRH learners and affiliates, such as Kiswahili, Arabic, or French.
3. Working comfort with Google Suites, Microsoft Outlook, Slack, WhatsApp Business, Project Management tools, and/or CRM platforms.

title: Europe Programme Officer - Balkans
body:
**Job Title :** Europe Programme Officer - Balkans

**Reports To:** Europe Regional Manager  
**Status:** Full-Time  
**Direct Reports:** Interns/volunteers, where relevant. (At present, this role doesn’t have direct reports)  
**Contract duration:** One year with the possibilities of extension depending on funding.  
**Compensation:** EUR 30,000 to 40,000 per year depending on location and experience.  
**Location** : IDC is remote-first, with office-based or co-working arrangements available in some countries. Candidates must already have the legal right to reside and work in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Greece, Kosovo\*, Montenegro, North Macedonia or Serbia. IDC cannot sponsor work permits or support relocation.

**Background**

International Detention Coalition (IDC) is a unique global network of over 200 civil society organisations and individuals in more than 75 countries, which coordinates with members and partners on advocacy, research, coalition and capacity building, to eliminate immigration detention and advance rights-based alternatives to detention.

**Role Purpose**

We are seeking a highly organised and motivated individual with a solid background in advocacy on migration and human rights and a strong understanding of the Western Balkans context. The ideal candidate will coordinate projects and events efficiently, contribute to strategic advocacy efforts and support the development of the capacity of IDC members and partners. Strong communications, organisational, planning, and stakeholder engagement skills are essential.

**Role Summary**

The Europe Programme Officer - Balkans will play a key role in supporting IDC’s mission in the Balkans and the wider IDC Europe programme. Working closely with the Europe Regional Manager and with other team members, the Programme Officer will contribute to regional programmes, events and advocacy strategies, while providing operational, administrative, research and communications support. The role will also help strengthen networks with members, partners, decision makers and other key stakeholders across the Balkans and wider Europe. The Programme Officer should be available to travel as needed.

**Role Responsibilities**

**Project implementation, admin support and support to IDC members and partners**

- Contribute to the implementation of national and regional projects and events in the Balkans including Greece and wider Europe by providing technical, administrative, and logistical support to the Europe Regional Programme and in collaboration with relevant IDC staff and members.
- Support the overall implementation of IDC’s mission and strategic priorities in the Europe region, with a particular focus on the Balkans, through a balance of operational efficiency and advocacy engagement.
- Support IDC’s members and partners in the Balkans and Europe, including through network building and capacity strengthening activities.
- Maintain a high level of organisation in managing project timelines, deliverables, and follow-ups in coordination with the Europe Regional Manager.
- Support administrative processes related to finances and other relevant areas in the Europe Programme, including the Balkans portfolio.

**Advocacy and Stakeholder Engagement**

- Support the development and implementation of advocacy strategies related to immigration detention, alternatives to detention, and broader migrant and refugee rights, focusing on national contexts in target countries in the Balkans.
- Support IDC’s advocacy in relation to the European Union and its institutions where relevant to the Western Balkans accession processes, including monitoring EU migration and asylum policy, enlargement and accession-related developments, and contributing to coordinated advocacy with national, regional and European networks and partners.
- In coordination with the Europe Regional Manager and other relevant team members, engage effectively with a wide range of stakeholders, including national and local government representatives, civil society actors, UN agencies, regional agencies, organisations and networks, to build partnerships and advance shared objectives.
- Contribute to drafting and disseminating advocacy materials, briefing notes, and strategic communications tailored to diverse audiences across the Balkans and wider Europe.
- Support research, data collection and evidence gathering on immigration detention and rights-based alternatives in the Balkans, to inform IDC’s advocacy, communications and programming.
- Maintain regular contact with IDC members and partners in the Balkans and Europe to identify policy gaps, advocacy opportunities, and spaces for support, partnership and coordinated action.
- Assist in the planning and facilitation of stakeholder consultations, trainings, and regional events that promote rights-based alternatives, pathways and regional dialogue in the Balkans.

**Communication**

- Assist with developing print and digital communication materials for the Balkans, including social media material for different platforms.
- Disseminate and share resources among members through different platforms.
- Contribute to monitoring media platforms and keep track of reports and updates on relevant developments in the Balkans and wider Europe.

**Internal Systems, Monitoring, Fundraising, and Institutional Support**

- Actively contribute to IDC’s fundraising efforts by providing background research, identifying potential funders, coordinating inputs, and playing an active role in the drafting of proposals aligned with Balkans and wider regional priorities.
- Ensure accurate and timely monitoring and reporting of programmatic activities, supporting internal evaluation processes and donor accountability in line with IDC’s MEL systems and relevant funders requirements.
- Maintain organised records of project outcomes, stakeholder engagement, and communications to support institutional memory and knowledge sharing.
- Assist in the preparation of high-quality reports, updates, and documentation for internal use, funders, and external dissemination.
- Support budget tracking, planning, and financial monitoring processes in collaboration with the Regional Manager, Executive Director, and relevant IDC team members.

**Core Responsibilities**

- Actively contribute to a culture of collaboration, teamwork, and support within the IDC team.
- Demonstrate a passion for and alignment with IDC’s mission, vision and core values of innovation, collaboration, respect, representation and being solutions-focused.
- Demonstrate an understanding of IDC policies including IDC Children and Vulnerable Adults Safeguarding policy to ensure a positive and safe working environment for all.
- Actively engage with organisational systems, processes, and infrastructure to ensure sustainability and appropriate safeguarding of institutional knowledge, assets and core activities over time.

**Key Selection Criteria**

**Essential Criteria**

- Demonstrated understanding of the European context, and specifically in the Balkans including Greece, particularly related to migration, asylum, human rights, and advocacy, including familiarity with national policy and legislative processes, regional cooperation mechanisms, and relevant EU accession and enlargement processes.
- Direct experience of advocacy or engagement with governments, institutions and civil society in the Balkans, and/or with EU institutions on migration, asylum or enlargement-related processes.
- A university degree in a relevant field such as international relations, law, migration studies, political science, social sciences or equivalent.
- A minimum of three years of professional experience, including project coordination, stakeholder engagement, and advocacy in the migration and/or human rights sectors, with relevant experience in the Balkans.
- Demonstrated experience in reporting, monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL), stakeholder engagement, and supporting advocacy initiatives with civil society, government and international partners.
- Strong communication, writing, organisational and coordination skills, with experience in planning and delivering meetings, workshops and other events.
- Ability to work independently in a remote environment, using initiative to manage competing priorities, meet deadlines and maintain a high level of attention to detail.
- Proficiency in using digital communication tools and platforms, including social media.
- Ability to undertake travel in the Balkans and wider Europe for the role.
- Residing in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Greece, Kosovo\*, Montenegro, North Macedonia or Serbia.
- Fluency in English (written and spoken) is mandatory.
- Strong commitment to IDC’s mission and values, including its safeguarding and child protection principles.

**Desirable Criteria**

- Experience working within networks or coalitions, including facilitating collaboration and peer learning among diverse member organisations.
- Knowledge of immigration detention and rights-based alternatives to detention in the Western Balkans context.
- Proficiency in Serbian and/or Albanian is a strong asset.
- Experience in regional cooperation mechanisms is a strong asset.
