title: Head of Support Services - Caracas
body:
The Danish Refugee Council is one of the world's leading humanitarian NGOs, working in over 30 countries to provide adequate assistance and protection to refugees, asylum seekers, IDPs, returnees, people on the move, and vulnerable local populations/host communities. Currently, DRC is seeking a highly qualified Head of Support Services, based in Caracas, Venezuela.

**About the job:** DRC is managing its operations in Venezuela under the direction of the country office in Caracas and four field offices located in the states of Sucre, Apure, and Zulia (Maracaibo and Santa Barbara de Zulia). DRC Venezuela is implementing an integrated Action encompassing the Protection, Food Security & Livelihood, WASH and Disaster Preparedness sectors.

**The overall purpose of the role**:

The Head of Support Services (HoSS) provides strategic leadership and oversight of all support functions, ensuring efficient, compliant, and accountable operations across the country programme. As a key member of the Senior Management Team, the HoSS leads Finance, Human Resources, Supply Chain and Procurement, Administration, IT, and Risk & Compliance functions, ensuring that DRC policies, procedures, and donor requirements are consistently applied and that operational capacities effectively support programme delivery.

The role contributes to the development and implementation of country strategies, translating organizational priorities into effective operational plans and systems. The HoSS provides technical guidance and strategic direction to support teams across the country operation, while fostering strong coordination with national authorities on regulatory, fiscal, labour, administrative, and customs-related matters.

Operating within one of DRC's largest and most complex country programmes, the HoSS oversees support functions across multiple locations, manages diverse donor compliance requirements, and ensures operational readiness in both emergency response and long-term programming contexts. The position requires a strategic and solutions-oriented leader capable of making sound decisions in dynamic environments, anticipating risks, driving continuous improvement, and upholding the highest standards of accountability, stewardship, and transparency.

**Responsibilities:**

**Management**

- Lead and manage the support managers (including people planning, performance, well-being and development).
- Manage, deliver and report on current operations programme support in Venezuela.
- Establish high performing support teams ensuring high-quality approaches are maintained.
- Develop and improve operational approaches, compliance and systems, and support the Country Director to build and deliver effective and sustainable interventions.
- Responsible for the strategic development, management and implementation of the support operations.
- Ensure appropriate technical support is available to programmes, in line with organisational priorities.
- Ensure support for annual planning and review processes.
- Direct responsibility for ensuring that the DRC programme operates in accordance with DRC’s support function guidelines.

**Operational Management**

- Support the Country Director and the Senior Management Team in liaising with donors and with national authorities, especially on issues of compliance, registration, taxation, labour law and audit.
- Oversee the operational support units for the country by providing strategic leadership and technical support to the areas under his/her supervision.
- Supervision, audits and controlling and implementation of corrective actions related to DRC’s operational standards within support area.
- Ensure that DRC retains and continually develops its operational capacity to provide rapid emergency response in particular within its procurement and transport systems.
- Develop, maintain and regularly update the country risk register and risk management plan, identifying the major financial, operational, legal, fraud and reputational risks, and lead the implementation and monitoring of mitigation measures together with the SMT.
- Ensure that all administrative and legal-related systems are accurate and maintained.
- Work to build the capacity of the operational support staff throughout the operation though frequent in-service training sessions and mentoring support.
- Contribute to the development and implementation of DRC’s global development initiatives.

**Managing support services in a large and demanding operation**

- Lead treasury, cash and liquidity management in a multi-currency environment: rigorous forecasting and planning, safe custody and movement of funds, and appropriate payment and transfer arrangements, ensuring at all times full compliance with national regulations, DRC procedures and donor requirements, and with the financial integrity standards applicable to the organisation.
- Ensure systematic compliance with the regulatory, screening and due-diligence requirements applicable to DRC and to its donors, including vetting of suppliers, partners and staff, and timely internal escalation of any issue identified.
- Maintain DRC’s legal registration and its tax, labour, migration and administrative compliance fully up to date, in close coordination with the competent national authorities; monitor developments in the applicable framework and advise the Country Director on their operational and financial implications.
- Take and own operational decisions under time pressure and on the basis of incomplete or evolving information, documenting the options considered, the rationale and the residual risk accepted; and demonstrate clear judgement on when to decide, when to consult and when to escalate to the Country Director or HQ.
- Lead business continuity and contingency planning for support services, covering infrastructure, energy, connectivity, logistics, customs, transport and financial contingencies, ensuring that critical stocks, alternative suppliers and back-up procedures are in place, documented and periodically tested.
- Ensure support services can scale up and scale down rapidly in response to sudden-onset emergencies, anticipatory action triggers and changes in funding levels, including the correct and documented use of emergency procurement modalities, derogations and waivers.
- Lead the support-services set-up and consolidation of the newly established Caracas field base covering the earthquake emergency response, premises and warehousing, assets and fleet, surge recruitment and onboarding, procurement pipelines, cash and banking arrangements, and clear delegation of authority, ensuring the base becomes fully operational and compliant at emergency speed while remaining co-located with the country office.
- Ensure the support functions absorb and service the earthquake response caseload alongside the regular programme portfolio, including the deployment, contracting and administration of surge and EMPACT staff, without degrading compliance standards or the level of support provided to the existing field bases.
- Provide effective remote management and technical supervision to support staff in field bases located at considerable distance from the country office, through clear delegation of authority, simplified and context-adapted procedures, and routine verification and spot checks.
- Strengthen and monitor the financial, procurement and HR compliance of national implementing partners, balancing risk management with a partnership-based, capacity-strengthening approach.
- Lead the preparation, facilitation and follow-up of internal, donor and statutory audits across a diversified multi-donor portfolio, ensuring timely closure of audit recommendations and organisational learning.
- Lead prevention, early detection and response to fraud and irregularities within DRC’s own operations and support functions, ensuring that safe reporting channels are known and used, and supporting Code of Conduct processes as requested.
- Uphold duty of care for staff working under sustained workload: safe working conditions, wellbeing measures, workload management, and calm and consistent communication during demanding periods.
- Participate in the country crisis management team, ensuring that support functions continue to deliver during emergencies, operational incidents and periods of heightened demand.

**DRC Dynamics ERP System**

- Ensure ERP functionality is properly used by relevant staff.
- Apply reports and data analytics from DRC Dynamics to improve overall performance.
- Act as heavy user for most of the project and finance functionalities.

**Occupational Health and Safety**

- To know the progress, results and effectiveness of the actions undertaken in the implementation and improvement of the occupational health and safety management system.
- Comply with the legal requirements applicable to occupational health and safety in each of the processes that correspond to them.
- Actively participate in the implementation and improvement of the occupational health and safety management system.
- Comply with and enforce the established programs and plans of the occupational health and safety management system.
- Maintain permanent feedback on the processes, plans and programs for which they are responsible through the implementation of corrective, preventive and improvement actions.
- Suspend any activity when it is determined that it is not complied with current and/or internal legal regulations related to occupational health and safety or endangers the integrity of the same.
- Actively participate in the development of the action plans of its competence in Occupational Health and Safety.
- Properly use the resources provided by the company in conjunction with the ARL for education and training in occupational safety and health.
- Properly use the equipment, tools and personal protection elements provided by the company.
- Truthfully report the state of health before, during and after the execution of the tasks for which they were hired.
- Actively participate in the identification of unsafe actions or conditions in workplaces.

Within their line management mandate, and in alignment with DRC’s leadership standards and policies, the position holder is responsible for:

- Providing leadership and direction to a team, ensuring clarity of roles, expectations, and performance standards to achieve agreed goals and objectives.
- Exercising team budget oversight and decision-making authority where assigned.
- Leading or contributing to recruitment processes for staff within their team and implementing termination decisions in accordance with DRC’s two-step principle.
- Conducting and/or signing off on performance appraisals and ensuring regular, constructive feedback to support continuous improvement.
- Supporting the professional development of team members through coaching, capacity building, and development planning.
- Addressing poor performance and disciplinary issues, including handling Code of Conduct cases referred to management, in line with DRC policies and procedures.

Within Technical Supervision mandate in the assigned thematic area and geographic scope, the position holder is responsible for:

- Providing technical direction, guidance, and where mandated, instructions to ensure compliance with DRC policies, standards, and strategies.
- Supporting managers and technical staff through regular communication, capacity building, and promotion of best practices.
- Support managers with assessing the technical skills and performance of most senior technical staff in the country and field offices.
- Escalating and, where authorized, addressing issues of non-compliance or poor performance in line with the technical supervision mandate.
- Participating in the recruitment of most senior technical staff in country and field offices.

**Experience and technical competencies:**

- At least 7 years’ experience in relevant field
- At least 4 years’ experience with people management.
- Experience in a similar role in an international NGO.
- Master’s degree in business administration, finance, supply chain management, international development, economics or another relevant field. A professional qualification in accounting, audit or supply chain (e.g. ACCA, CIMA, CPA, CIPS) is an asset. Equivalent professional experience in support services management in complex operations may be considered.
- Proven leadership skills and competence in people management.
- Proven operational management experience and capability in large and complex operations with demanding financial, logistical and compliance environments, including multi-currency settings.
- Proven significant financial, information and systems management experience.
- Significant experience in procurement and tender processes.
- Understanding and experience of institutional fundraising.
- Experience working in an ERP system, including supply chain, finance and HR systems.
- Demonstrated ability to take sound and timely decisions under pressure, with incomplete information and shifting parameters, and to be accountable for them.
- Proven experience in treasury and cash management in multi-currency environments and in operations with a significant cash component.
- Demonstrated working knowledge of the regulatory, screening and due-diligence requirements applicable to humanitarian organisations and their donors.
- Experience leading donor, internal and statutory audits and managing compliance across a diversified multi-donor portfolio.
- Experience working through, and strengthening the compliance capacity of, national implementing partners.
- Experience in business continuity planning, crisis management and rapid scale-up or scale-down of support functions.
- Demonstrated experience in opening, setting up or rapidly reinforcing field bases and support systems in response to sudden-onset emergencies (earthquakes, floods, mass displacement).
- Proven ability to lead, motivate and hold accountable dispersed teams managed remotely.
- Full professional proficiency in English and Spanish

**We offer:**

- The opportunity to be part of one of the best NGOs worldwide.
- Access to over 1,000 free online trainings and certifications.
- Contract duration: 1 year contract renewable based on funding availability and satisfactory performance
- Salary: Under the band E Management, level 1.Terms of Employment for national or expatriate staff, as applicable.
- Health Insurance

title: Caseworker (Dari speaking)
body:
**IRC Background:** The mission of the International Rescue Committee (IRC) is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC has a presence in over 40 countries and 27 offices in the United States; the IRC leads the way from harm to home. Domestically, our offices across the U.S. ensure new arrivals have food, shelter, and clothing, and work with refugees to help them gain self-sufficiency.

**Job Overview:** The UHP Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other qualified immigrants to support a positive resettlement experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The UHP Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure each client has living essentials such as housing, food, medical care, and access to transportation, and is oriented to their new environment.
- Provide comprehensive, client-centered case management services including but not limited to accessing public benefits, housing, mental health services, medical care, school and ESL enrollment, referrals to community service providers, and assistance with booking appointments and scheduling transportation and interpretation.
- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Work cross different programs as needed
- Other duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position reports to:** OIRS Casework Supervisor

**Position directly supervises:** N/A

**Indirect Reporting: Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

***Internal:***IRC Employees and program departments across Sacramento

***External:***IRC partners and other community agencies

**Job Requirements:**

- Associate or BA degree with an emphasis in Social Work, Migration Studies, Public Health, Refugee Studies, Development, Immigration Law, or an equivalent field of study; or 1+ years of related professional experience; preferably with asylum-seeking families, refugees, internally displaced persons, or individuals without status.
- Relevant professional experience in human services field required; minimum of 2 years’ experience strongly preferred.
- Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations strongly preferred.
- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written; proficiency Dari/Farsi and Pashto spoken by IRC’s clients.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.
- Commitment to teamwork and collaboration across all of IRC’s programs.
- Understanding of the U.S. immigration system and the rights of immigrants.
- Comfortability collaborating with governmental agencies and community providers.
- Ability to maintain accurate and up-to-date physical and electronic files and detailed case notes, enter required data in a timely manner, meet all case reporting requirements within established timelines and standards.
- Excellent writing and organizational skills with the ability to effectively summarize large amounts of information and maintain records of case progress achieved
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- This position will work from the IRC office in Sacramento.
- Offices hours are scheduled as Monday-Friday, 9:00am-5pm.

***This position is expected to end on September 30, 2027.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $29.10 - $30/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written; proficiency Ukrainian or Russian spoken by IRC’s clients.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.
- Commitment to teamwork and collaboration across all of IRC’s programs.
- Understanding of the U.S. immigration system and the rights of immigrants.
- Comfortability collaborating with governmental agencies and community providers.
- Ability to maintain accurate and up-to-date physical and electronic files and detailed case notes, enter required data in a timely manner, meet all case reporting requirements within established timelines and standards.
- Excellent writing and organizational skills with the ability to effectively summarize large amounts of information and maintain records of case progress achieved
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- This position will work from the IRC office in Sacramento.
- Offices hours are scheduled as Monday-Friday, 9:00am-5pm.

***This position is expected to end on September 30, 2027.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $29.10 - $30/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Country Director - Yemen, Sana'a
body:
**Who are we?**

The Danish Refugee Council (DRC) is one of the world's leading humanitarian organizations, working to protect, advocate for, and promote durable solutions for people affected by displacement, conflict, and crisis. Across the Middle East, Asia, and Europe, DRC delivers integrated humanitarian and development programming that addresses immediate needs while supporting longer-term resilience and recovery.

Yemen is one of DRC's largest, most complex, and strategically important operations globally. With a presence in the country since 2008 and a significant scale-up following the onset of the current conflict in 2015, DRC has established itself as a leading humanitarian actor responding to one of the world's most protracted humanitarian crises. Operating from a Country Office in Sana'a and through an extensive field presence across Aden, Dhamar, Hajjah, Hodeidah, Mokha, Sa'dah, Shabwa, and Taizz, DRC delivers life-saving and resilience-building assistance to vulnerable communities affected by conflict, displacement, and mixed migration.

DRC's diverse portfolio spans emergency response, protection, camp coordination and camp management (CCCM), economic recovery, shelter and non-food items (NFI), water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), humanitarian mine action, and mixed migration programming. With an annual programme portfolio of approximately USD 100 million, Yemen represents one of DRC's largest country programmes, offering a unique opportunity to lead a highly visible and impactful operation at scale.

**Overall purpose of the role**

The Country Director provides strategic leadership to one of DRC's largest and most complex country operations, driving DRC's comprehensive and solutions-oriented approach to displacement in one of the world's most challenging humanitarian contexts. The role requires visionary leadership, innovation, strong external representation, and effective advocacy to position DRC as a leading humanitarian actor and trusted partner in Yemen.

As DRC's senior representative in the country, the Country Director is ultimately accountable for all aspects of the organization's operations, including programme quality, safety and security, people management, financial stewardship, risk management, compliance, and external relations. The Country Director leads both the consolidation and continued development of the Yemen programme, strengthening impact measurement, accountability to affected populations, and organizational effectiveness while ensuring that operational models remain responsive to a dynamic and complex environment.

The Country Director sets strategic direction, inspires and develops high-performing teams, safeguards staff welfare and security, and fosters a culture of collaboration, accountability, and learning. Through effective delegation and oversight, the role ensures that DRC's substantial resources are managed responsibly and that humanitarian assistance is delivered with the highest standards of quality, integrity, and impact.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

**Leadership and Management**

Within their line management mandate, and in alignment with DRC's Leadership Standards and organizational policies, the Country Director is responsible for:

- Providing overall leadership, strategic direction, and management of DRC's country operation.
- Leading, supporting, and developing the Senior Management Team to ensure effective collaboration, sound decision-making, and achievement of strategic and operational objectives.
- Establishing clear objectives, expectations, and accountability across the country operation and promoting a culture aligned with DRC's values and Leadership Standards.
- Exercising delegated budget and management authority in accordance with DRC policies and procedures.
- Ensuring that recruitment, performance management, staff development, succession planning, and disciplinary processes are implemented effectively and in accordance with DRC policies.
- Fostering staff wellbeing, engagement, and professional development while ensuring DRC's duty of care obligations are met.
- Addressing performance, conduct, and Code of Conduct matters in line with DRC policies and procedures.

**Representation**

- Represent DRC at national, regional, and international levels with government authorities, donors, UN agencies, diplomatic missions, NGOs, consortium partners, and other key stakeholders.
- Strengthen DRC's strategic positioning, reputation, and influence in Yemen.
- Ensure that DRC maintains effective and constructive relationships with displacement-affected communities, authorities, donors, partners, and the wider humanitarian and development community.
- Promote DRC's integrated and solutions-oriented approach to displacement and actively contribute to humanitarian coordination and policy dialogue.

**Strategic Leadership and Operational Oversight**

- Provide overall management oversight of the country programme and ensure strategic coherence across programme and support functions.
- Directly line manage designated senior staff and ensure that the Senior Management Team functions as an effective leadership body.
- Ensure appropriate organizational structures, systems, and resources are in place to support programme delivery and operational effectiveness.
- Maintain regular engagement with field operations through frequent field visits, providing leadership support, oversight, and representation.
- Ensure compliance with all internal governance, risk management, and reporting requirements.

**Fundraising and Advocacy**

- Lead donor engagement, strategic partnerships, and resource mobilization efforts to sustain and grow the country portfolio.
- Ensure strong donor relations and high-quality donor engagement throughout the programme cycle.
- Lead the implementation of DRC's advocacy priorities and ensure advocacy initiatives are informed by operational evidence, programme learning, and protection concerns.
- Promote principled humanitarian action and amplify the voices and priorities of displacement-affected populations in relevant forums.

**Safety**

- Hold overall accountability for safety, security, and duty of care across the country operation.
- Ensure effective security management systems and procedures are maintained and adapted to the evolving context.
- Oversee security analysis, risk management, preparedness, and crisis response mechanisms to support informed decision-making and safe programme delivery.

**Support Services and Financial Management**

- Hold overall accountability for the financial health, sustainability, and compliance of the country operation.
- Work closely with the Head of Support Services to ensure effective financial planning, budget management, internal controls, and risk management systems.
- Ensure that all resources are managed effectively, responsibly, and in compliance with DRC policies, donor requirements, and relevant legal obligations.
- Ensure that support functions provide timely, efficient, and compliant services that enable high-quality programme implementation.
- Promote capacity development and continuous improvement across all support functions.

**Programme Development and Quality**

- Lead the development, implementation, and review of the country strategy in alignment with DRC's global and regional strategic frameworks.
- Ensure programmes are evidence-based, responsive to context and needs, and contribute to DRC's strategic objectives and solutions-oriented approach to displacement.
- Promote innovation, learning, and adaptive management to maximize programme quality and impact.
- Support the development of integrated, multi-sectoral programming that strengthens protection outcomes and contributes to durable solutions.

**Accountability and Compliance**

- Ensure adherence to DRC policies, standards, and procedures, including the Code of Conduct, safeguarding commitments, DRC Operations Handbook, and donor compliance requirements.
- Promote accountability to affected populations and ensure communities meaningfully inform programme design and implementation.
- Ensure consistent application of DRC's Programme Cycle Management framework to strengthen programme quality, accountability, monitoring, evaluation, and learning.
- Foster a culture of accountability, compliance, learning, and continuous improvement across the country operation.

**Experience and technical competencies:**

To be successful in this role we expect you to have minimum five years’ management experience in emergency/development contexts as country director/senior manager of a humanitarian or development organization or similar, moreover, we also expect the following:

- Experience as a people manager;
- Experience representing a large and leading organization to donors, external partners and authorities;
- Experience with networking, advocacy and coordination;
- Experience in managing staff in insecure/stressful locations;
- Experience with conflict related displacement issues;
- Experience of managing budgets and multiple donor contracts;
- Experience in donor contact, fundraising and networking;
- Experience of Humanitarian Mine Action (preferred);
- Experience working in the Middle East region and Yemen (preferred);
- Proven leadership skills and competence in people management;
- Proven communicator with all types of stakeholders; and
- Proven commitment to accountable practices and knowledge of quality assurance systems.

**Languages**

- English is required
- Arabic is desirable

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:

- **Striving for excellence**: You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating**: You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead**: You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating**: You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity**: Upholding and promoting the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to DRC’s values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**Education:**

- Master’s degree in relevant field

**We offer**

Contract length: 12 months contract

Position Band: This position will be placed at Management band (D)

Suggested Start date: January 01, 2027

Duty station: Yemen, Sana’a

Designation of Duty Station: Unaccompanied / Non-family duty station

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for Expatriates or Nationals.

title: Research Officer
Referral for Migrants and Mobile Populations Consultant
body:
Position Title : **Referral for Migrants and Mobile Populations Consultant**

Duty Station : IOM Philippines Country Office (Cotabato)

Classification: Consultant

Type of Appointment: Consultancy

Estimated Start Date: ASAP

Closing Date : 8 October 2026

**Project Context and Scope**

AThe International Organization for Migration (IOM)’s health program in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) aims at strengthening the resilience and responsiveness of the region’s health system and improving access to healthcare, as part of the organization’s strategy to alleviate the driver of unwanted migration and to reduce health-related risks during displacements and migration cycle. IOM has implemented various health-related projects that contributed to better health outcomes in the BARMM.

IOM’s project “Building Resilience through Inclusive Governance and Healthcare Transformation in BARMM (BRIGHT-BARMM), funded by Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA), aims to enhance the local capacity of Ministry of Health (MOH), the local provinces and cities/municipalities, to pursue key and cross cutting reforms in health systems. It will strengthen Health Systems (HS), particularly in areas of health governance and leadership, financing, and data and information, to provide a more conducive setting for implementing Safe Motherhood (SM), Adolescent Reproductive Health (ARH), and Global Health Security (GHS) programs.

Within the GHS component, IOM seeks to strengthen the capacity of the government, health workers, and frontline workers to promote inclusive, preventive, and culturally and gender appropriate health programs for returning migrants and mobile populations. This includes improving access to health information, strengthening referral pathways, and reducing the potential spread of infectious diseases through Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) materials, capacity-building of health workers at Points of Entry (PoEs), and the establishment of referral pathways to strengthen access to screening, counselling, and treatment for returnees and migrants. To support these efforts, IOM will engage a consultant to provide advisory and technical assistance with a focus on Referral Pathways for Returning Migrants and Mobile Populations.

Under the overall guidance of the Head of Sub-Office in Cotabato City, direct supervision of the National Migration Health Programme Coordinator, and in collaboration with the technical leads, the successful candidate will produce analytical papers, finalize the Referral Pathway Toolkit and SOP Manual, and facilitate the development of a Referral Pathway Institutionalization and Sustainability Plan. These outputs will contribute to strengthening national and local capacity to promote inclusive, preventive, and rights-based health programmes for returnees and host communities in areas of return and reintegration.

The objective of this consultancy is to strengthen migration health referral systems in ZamBaSulTa by refining and institutionalizing referral pathways, developing standardized referral tools and SOPs, building the capacity of stakeholders through training and mentoring, and establishing sustainable coordination and governance mechanisms to improve access to health, protection, and other essential services for Returning Filipinos from Sabah (ReFS), migrants and mobile populations.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing**  
Migration Health Unit in Mindanao

BRIGHT BARMM: MA1161: 3:3:1:006-Consultancy (inc. CP) Migration Health

## **Responsibilities**

**Tasks to be performed under this contract**

**A**. **FIRST DELIVERABLES:** Migration Health Referral Pathway Refinement, Validation, and Operationalization Package

Building on the outputs and recommendations generated during the completed consultation and validation workshop, the consultant shall:

- Review existing and initially drafted health referral systems, protocols, service mapping outputs, and draft referral pathway tools developed under the project, identifying gaps, overlaps, and opportunities for strengthening alignment with national, BARMM, and local referral mechanisms.
- Refine and validate Migration Health Referral Pathway Package for ZamBaSulTa, ensuring that it is practical, context-specific, gender-responsive, protection-sensitive, and responsive to the health and protection needs of Returning Filipinos from Sabah (ReFs), migrants, and mobile populations. The package shall include, at a minimum:
    - Referral pathway flowcharts and process maps;
    - Standardized referral and feedback forms;
    - Referral tracking and monitoring tools;
    - Service mapping and directory templates;
    - Roles and responsibilities matrix for participating agencies and service providers; and
    - Referral coordination and reporting mechanisms.
- Prepare a draft Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) Manual to support the implementation and institutionalization of the referral pathway. The SOP shall clearly define procedures for:
    - Identification and screening of referral cases;
    - Referral initiation, acceptance, and case handover;
    - Follow-up and closure of referral cases;
    - Health, protection, and multisectoral referral coordination;
    - Confidentiality, informed consent, and data-sharing protocols;
    - Documentation, reporting, and referral monitoring requirements; and
    - Roles and responsibilities of Bangsamoro Migration Health Network (BMHN) members and other relevant stakeholders.

-Activities shall be completed by 30 October 2026, with all required deliverable reports submitted by email to IOM no later than 30 November 2026 (30% of overall contract value)

**B. SECOND DELIVERABLES:** Referral Pathway Training Package and Capacity Building

Building on the refined Migration Health Referral Pathway Package and draft SOPs, the consultant shall develop and deliver a comprehensive capacity-building programme to support the effective implementation, institutionalization, and sustainability of referral mechanisms for migrants, ReFs, and mobile populations in ZamBaSulTa.

The consultant shall:

- Co-develop with the RCCE Consultant the refinement of the training design, curriculum, agenda, and learning materials for the RCCE and Referral Pathway Training to strengthen the capacity of stakeholders serving returning migrants and mobile populations.
- Develop a comprehensive Migration Health Referral Pathway Training Package, ensuring that all materials are culturally sensitive, gender-/age-/ability-inclusive, and accessible to the diverse stakeholders involved in referral management and service delivery. The package shall include, at a minimum:
    - Facilitator's Guide
    - Participant's Manual
    - Presentation materials
    - Pre- and post-training assessment tools
    - Case studies and practical referral scenarios
    - Referral pathway simulation and tabletop exercises
- Conduct a training workshop for Bangsamoro Migration Health Network (BMHN) members, frontline POE workers, local health workers in referral facilities in ZamBaSulTa, and other service providers on referral pathways. Using the training materials and package developed, and referencing the IOM Health, Border, and Mobility Management (HBMM) framework, DOH/MOH referral structure, IOM Protection Handbook, and Sphere standards, the sessions shall cover, as applicable, the following topics:
- Understanding the migrant context and mobility patterns of ZamBaSulTa, including, informal and irregular movements of Returning Filipinos from Sabah (REFs)
- Health risk identification and prioritization, facilitating and institutionalizing referral pathways, and monitoring and tracking of referral cases.
- Monitoring and evaluation on the effectiveness of referral pathway, and implementing continuous improvement to maintain effective referral
- Prepare and submit a Training Completion Report summarizing the training methodology, participant profile, pre- and post-training assessment results, key findings, recommendations, and proposed actions to support the operationalization and institutionalization of the migration health referral pathway in ZamBaSulTa.

-Activities shall be completed by 30 November 2026, with all required deliverable reports submitted by email to IOM no later than 30 December 2026 (30% of overall contract value)

**C**. **THIRD DELIVERABLES:** Finalization, Institutionalization, and Handover Package

Building on the validated Migration Health Referral Pathway Package, SOPs, and capacity-building activities, the consultant shall finalize all technical outputs and support their institutionalization for sustained implementation by the BMHN and relevant stakeholders.

The consultant shall:

- Finalize and integrate all revisions arising from stakeholder consultations, validation workshops, training activities, and technical reviews into the Migration Health Referral Pathway Package, ensuring consistency, usability, and alignment with national, BARMM, and local referral systems.
- Finalize the Referral Pathway Toolkit, including referral flowcharts, standardized referral and feedback forms, referral tracking and monitoring tools, service mapping directories, coordination mechanisms, and roles and responsibilities matrices.
- Finalize the Referral Pathway SOP Manual and incorporate recommendations to support institutional adoption, implementation, monitoring, and sustainability of referral mechanisms for migrants, Returning Filipinos from Sabah (ReFs), and mobile populations in ZamBaSulTa.
- Develop a Referral Pathway Institutionalization and Sustainability Plan outlining recommended governance arrangements, coordination structures, monitoring and reporting mechanisms, capacity development needs, and actions required to support the long-term operationalization of the referral system through the partner agencies.
- Prepare and submit all final digital reports and outputs in editable formats to facilitate future reproduction, updating, dissemination, and utilization by BMHN, MOH-BARMM, local government units, and relevant stakeholders.
- Present the final referral pathway package and key recommendations to IOM through a turnover and dissemination session.

-Activities shall be completed by 30 December 2026, with all required deliverable reports submitted by email to IOM no later than 15 January 2027 (40% of overall contract value)

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

- The Consultant’s performance will be assessed based on the timely completion, quality, and comprehensiveness of the agreed deliverables, as well as the effectiveness of technical assistance, stakeholder coordination, and documentation and reporting.
- Percentage of task completion specified in the ToR based on supervisors’ performance evaluation. Tasks are divided into technical assistance (60%), coordination, liaison, and networking to National, Regional, and Local stakeholders and partners (10%), documentation and reporting (30%).
- Relevance of planning, organization and timeliness for managing and delivering progress reports and outputs.
- Practical applicability and institutional adoption by BMHN and relevant government partners.
- Timeliness and completeness of deliverable
- Feedback from stakeholders on the quality of work and reports.
- Contribution to achieving project goals and objectives in BARMM, such as strengthened operational and institutional capacity and guidelines or policies, BARMM application of new knowledge, and effective service delivery.

## **Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

- Master’s or Higher degree in Public Health, Health Systems Management, Global Health, Sociology, Communications, Emergency/ Disaster Management, Health Systems/Operations, or any related field from an accredited academic institution with ten years of relevant professional experience.
- Advanced knowledge and proven experience in public health, global health security and migration health.

Demonstrated experience on the following:

- Referral systems, health systems strengthening, case management, community health, health emergency preparedness and response, or related fields.
- Development and institutionalization of referral pathways, referral systems, SOPs, case management, coordination mechanisms, and service delivery protocols;
- Development of technical guidance documents, toolkits, manuals, analytical reports, and operational plans
- Migration Health programming, including addressing the health needs of migrants, returnees, displaced populations, and other mobile and vulnerable group;
- Experience in conducting RCCE training, would be an asset;
- Effective facilitation of stakeholder consultations, validation, and capacity-building activities is considered an asset.
- Experience working in complex health system environments, preferably in the Philippines or similar contexts, and strong understanding of Population Mobility Mapping, Health Mobility and Border Management, WHO Risk Communication and Community Engagement toolkits, Bangsamoro Migration Health Network and other international standards are desirable.
- Prior working experience with the International Organization, UN, Development Organization, National, and BARMM government is highly desirable.
- Familiarity with the issues, policies, structure, and context of the Global, Philippines, and Bangsamoro context on public health is highly desirable.
- Strong analytical, communication, and training skills are required to build capacity among health staff at various system levels effectively.
- Excellent analytical, report writing, facilitation, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills, with demonstrated ability to produce high-quality technical outputs and recommendations.

**Languages**

For this consultancy, English; Tagalog

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

**Values** - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

- **Inclusion and respect for diversity**: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- **Integrity and transparency**: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- **Professionalism**: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- **Courage**: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- **Empathy**: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

**Core Competencies** – behavioural indicators

- **Teamwork**: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- **Delivering results**: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- **Managing and sharing knowledge**: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- **Accountability**: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- **Communication**: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

**Notes**

IOM covers Consultants against occupational accidents and illnesses under the Compensation Plan (CP), free of charge, for the duration of the consultancy. IOM does not provide evacuation or medical insurance for reasons related to non-occupational accidents and illnesses. Consultants are responsible for their own medical insurance for non-occupational accident or illness and will be required to provide written proof of such coverage before commencing work.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

title: National Project Officer | Emergency Response | Roster only
body:
Position Title : **National Project Officer | Emergency Response | Roster only**

Duty Station : IOM Philippines Country Office

Classification: General Service, UG

Type of Appointment: Special Short-Term

Estimated Start Date: ASAP

Closing Date : 11 October 2026

This Call for Applications aims to establish **a roster of qualified candidates** who may be mobilized to support the Mission’s surge staffing requirements during disasters, emergencies, and other humanitarian response operations.

Please note that there is currently no confirmed start date or immediate deployment opportunity associated with this roster. The engagement of roster members will depend on operational requirements, the nature and scale of emergency responses, funding and budget availability, and the Mission’s staffing needs.

Candidates who submit an application acknowledge their interest in being considered for future emergency response assignments and are expected to maintain their availability should their services be required. If selected for deployment or engagement, roster members must be locally available and be prepared to promptly complete all necessary onboarding, documentation, and administrative requirements within the prescribed timeframe.

As part of your application, kindly **submit a cover letter** indicating any relevant experience in emergency response and/or the following areas: ***Shelter, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Cash-Based Interventions (CBI), Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), Community Mobilization, Information Management and Reporting, and Health.*** Your cover letter should briefly describe your experience, key responsibilities, and any relevant skills or training related to these areas.

## **Responsibilities**

3. ​Participate in the development and adjustment of work plans, project budgets, Monitoring & Evaluation tools and standard operations procedures.
4. ​Coordinate the collection, verification and analysis of data and background information; update information management systems and social media platforms on project related activities including project awareness and visibility, summaries, press releases and other relevant materials.
5. ​Coordinate timely preparation and dissemination of project reports in accordance with IOM procedures and donor requirements.
6. ​Liaise and coordinate with donors, partners, United Nations agencies, local authorities and stakeholders and government counterparts.
7. ​Contribute to the planning, development, organization and delivery of capacity building activities targeting IOM staff, government and civil society partners, implementing partners and communities.
8. ​Attend relevant working groups, interagency coordination meetings, and other forums.
9. ​Supervise and provide technical guidance to project staff.
10. ​Undertake duty travel relating to project implementation, monitoring visits, project assessments, liaison with counterparts, etc.
11. ​Perform other related duties as required. ​

## **Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

- ​​Bachelor’s degree in Political or Social Sciences, International Relations, Development Studies, Migration Studies, Human Rights, Law or related fields from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or,
- ​Master’s degree in the above-mentioned fields

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- ​​Experience in liaising with governmental authorities, national/international institutions, United Nations agencies and non-governmental organizations;
- ​Experience in working with migrants, refugees, internally displaced persons, victims of trafficking and other vulnerable groups; and,
- ​Prior work experience with international humanitarian organizations, non-government or government institutions/organization in a multi-cultural setting is an advantage.

**Skills**

- ​​Extensive experience in implementing or overseeing humanitarian or emergency response operations.
- ​Demonstrated ability to interact with national- and/or regional-level government counterparts, donors, and inter-agency clusters.
- ​Experience in working with Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and other vulnerable groups.
- ​Prior work experience with international humanitarian organizations, non-government or government institutions/organization in a multi-cultural setting is an advantage.​

**Languages**

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position, Tagalog is required.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

- **Inclusion and respect for diversity**: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- **Integrity and transparency**: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- **Professionalism**: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- **Courage**: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.

- **Accountability**: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.

**Notes**

This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.

As part of your application, kindly **submit a cover letter** indicating any relevant experience in emergency response and/or the following areas: ***Shelter, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Cash-Based Interventions (CBI), Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), Community Mobilization, and Information Management and Reporting.*** Your cover letter should briefly describe your experience, key responsibilities, and any relevant skills or training related to these areas.

## **Responsibilities**

1. Assist in the planning, coordination, implementation, and monitoring of emergency response activities, ensuring timely and effective delivery of humanitarian assistance in line with project objectives, humanitarian principles, and donor requirements.
2. Compile, analyse, and present information and data on disaster impacts, humanitarian needs, response operations, and operational developments to support evidence-based decision-making and response planning.
3. Monitor project budget implementation and resource utilization, identifying funding gaps and proposing adjustments to support efficient and accountable emergency response operations.
4. Serve as the focal point for administrative and operational coordination of emergency response activities, liaising with internal units and external stakeholders to facilitate procurement, logistics, deployments, clearances, and other operational requirements.
5. Prepare situation reports, implementation updates, and progress reports, identify operational challenges and delivery gaps, escalate critical issues to the supervisor, and recommend corrective actions to improve response effectiveness.
6. Draft correspondence, briefing notes, donor reports, presentations, maps, dashboards, statistical tables, and other operational documentation to support coordination, reporting, and decision-making during emergency response operations.
7. Organize and support coordination meetings, simulations, trainings, and capacity-building activities for government counterparts, humanitarian partners, and response personnel on emergency preparedness, response, and recovery.
8. Respond to complex operational information requests, maintain project records, and ensure accurate documentation of emergency response activities, beneficiary data, and operational outputs.
9. Participate in inter-agency coordination mechanisms and technical working groups, maintaining effective collaboration with government agencies, local authorities, UN agencies, humanitarian clusters, NGOs, donors, and other stakeholders to strengthen coordinated emergency response efforts.
10. Monitor the implementation of activities by implementing partners, ensuring compliance with project agreements, humanitarian standards, IOM policies, and donor requirements, and promptly report any issues to the supervisor.
11. Contribute to the development and revision of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), contingency plans, emergency response guidelines, after-action reviews, lessons learned, and concept notes to strengthen preparedness and future emergency response programming.
12. Provides guidance/training and assist in coordinating and monitoring work of other staff in the unit. May supervise other staff as assigned.
13. Perform such other relevant duties as maybe assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Social Science, International Relations, Development Studies, Migration Studies, Human Rights, Law or a related field from an accredited academic institution with four years of relevant professional experience; or,

- Experience in liaising with governmental authorities, national/international institutions, United Nations agencies and non-governmental organisations;
- Experience in working with migrants, refugees, internally displaced persons, victims of trafficking and other vulnerable groups; and,
- Prior work experience with international humanitarian organisations, non-government or government institutions/organisation in a multi-cultural setting is an advantage.

- Strong understanding of Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Climate Change Adaptation (CCA), and humanitarian principles and standards.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including technical and donor reporting.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Teams.

For this position, Tagalog is required.

- **Professionalism**: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
